INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry,
having been authorized by the Committee, hereby present this Two Hundred Thirty-Ninth Report
on Action Taken Notes furnished by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises on the
recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two Hundred Twenty-Ninth Report on the Credit
Facilities to MSME Sector.
2. I thank the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises for furnishing the Action
Taken Notes on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two Hundred Twenty-Ninth
Report.
3. The Committee in its meeting held on the 19
th March, 2013 considered and adopted the
Report.
TIRUCHI SIV A
NEW D ELHI; Chairman,
19th March, 2013 Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Industry.

1
REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two
Hundred Twenty-Ninth Report on the Credit Facilities to MSME sector pertaining to Ministry of
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.
2. Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium
Enterprises in respect of the recommendations contained in the Report. These have been
categorized as follows:
Chapter-I– The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry.
The Committee is pleased to observe that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations
as mentioned in the Chapter–I of the Report.
Chapter-II–  The recommendation/observations, which the Committee does not desire to
pursue in view of the Government’s replies.
In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic and
explanations advanced by the Ministry and therefore do not want to pursue them for the present.
Chapter-III–  The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee has
either not accepted replies of the Ministry or has asked the Ministry to review its reply.
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of recommendations
contained in Chapter–III and desires that the Ministry should furnish logical explanations therefore.
Chapter-IV–  The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the
Ministry have not been received.
In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished the
interim replies or couched its language in vague terms like noted for compliance/guidance,
therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respects
of recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention and
spirit of the recommendations of the Committee.
3. The details of the ATR are being discussed in the succeeding pages.

2
CHAPTER-I
Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry
Recommendation/observation
1. The Committee is of the view that as per RBI guidelines, credit flow to women
entrepreneurs must be augmented to bring more and more women to the mainstream of the
economic development. Keeping this in mind the women entrepreneurs should be allowed
loans on liberal and relaxed terms. (Para 3 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
On the above issue, the RBI has reported that to help overcome the hurdles being faced
by women in accessing bank credit and credit plus services, the Government had drawn up a
14-point action plan (now 13-point action plan) in the year 2000 for implementation by public
sector banks. The public sector banks were advised to earmark 5 per cent of their Adjusted Net
Bank Credit (ANBC) for lending to women. As on March 31, 2011, the amount outstanding
towards credit to women was Rs.1,82,667.41 crore forming 7.46 per cent of ANBC of public
sector banks. Out of 26 public sector banks, 23 banks have achieved the target of 5% of adjusted
net bank credit for lending to women. As at the end of March 2011, eleven public sector banks
have opened 31 specialized branches for women.
SIDBI provides credit assistance to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs),
including Women Entrepreneurs, to encourage them to do their business smoothly. In order to
encourage banks to provide collateral free loans to MSEs, the Government through Ministry of
MSME alongwith SIDBI set up the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
(CGTMSE) in 2000. The guarantee cover under the Credit Guarantee Scheme is at an enhanced
level of 80% for MSEs operated and/or owned by women entrepreneurs. Cumulatively, CGTMSE
as on March 31, 2012, has extended guarantee approvals to 1,40,369 women entrepreneurs
covering credit assistance of Rs. 5,618.06 crore.
To set up micro enterprises under Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme
(PMEGP), women entrepreneurs are entitled to a higher rate of margin money subsidy, viz.,
@ 35% in rural areas and @ 25% in urban areas in comparison to 25% and 15% respectively for
general category. Also women entrepreneurs are required to pay lower beneficiary contribution, viz.,
5% of the project cost in comparison to 10% for general category.
Further, IBA has informed that loans on liberal terms and special relaxation to women
entrepreneurs are considered by individual banks.
Recommendation/observation
2. Keeping in view the global development in industrial sector and the competition
which has resulted in the improved working of the banks, the Committee is of the view that
RBI should adopt more liberal approach to encourage the banks for opening branches
specifically in industrial belts. (Para 4 of ATN)
2

3
Action taken/Comments
The recommendation was taken up with the Department of Financial Services and also with
the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Indian Banks’ Association (IBA). However, specific
information relating to opening of branches in industrial belts has not been provided.
On the above issue the RBI has reported that with a view to facilitate branch opening the
branch authorisation policy for opening branches has been liberalized by RBI. Domestic scheduled
commercial banks (other than RRBs) are permitted to open branches/Mobile branches/
Administrative offices/Central Processing Centres (CPCs)/Service branches in Tier 3 to Tier 6
centres (with population upto 49,999 as per Census 2001) without permission from RBI in each
case, subject to reporting. Domestic scheduled commercial banks (other than RRBs) are also
permitted to open branches/Mobile branches/Administrative offices/Central Processing Centres
(CPCs)/Service branches in rural, semi-urban and urban centres in North Eastern States and Sikkim
without permission from RBI in each case, subject to reporting.
Recommendation/observation
3. The Committee endorses the cluster based approach for growth and expansion of the
MSME. The banks must deal with such clusters to reduce their transaction cost and improve
their infrastructure and other facilities. (Para 8 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
RBI has informed that the banks have been advised to adopt one cluster and explore the
financing requirements of units in such clusters. Further, all banks have been advised vide circular
dated June 29, 2010 that they should open more MSE focused branch offices at different MSE
clusters which can also act as Counselling Centres for MSEs. Each lead bank of a district may
adopt at least one MSE cluster.
MoMSME had forwarded to the Convenors of State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) the
list of 25 MSME clusters identified as innovative clusters, comprehensive list of 2,441 clusters in
the registered MSME sector as per Fourth All India Census of MSMEs (2006-07), list of 472
clusters taken up for development under Micro and Small Enterprises-Cluster Development
Programme (MSE-CDP) and based on field level information on bank branches existing in the
clusters, list of such MSME clusters indicating the banks/financial institutions in the clusters and
the position of available banking facilities, for displaying on website of SLBC Convenor banks so
that the banks operating in the State/UT come forward to provide necessary banking facilities/
services in these clusters. The Lead Banks in the districts where the MSME clusters are located
may focus on their credit requirements and enhance credit flow to MSMEs. The RBI has also
advised the SLBC Convenor banks in this regard.
SIDBI and its associates have adopted cluster based approach for providing credit and non-
credit support to the MSME sector which includes rendering technical services for technology
transfer, providing financial support including promotion of clean production, energy efficiency
measures, organising cluster development programme under its Promotional and Development
activities, etc.
Recommendation/observation
4. The Committee feels that each Bank should identify the branches having potential
for financing Micro and Small Enterprises for greater credit flow to this critical sector.
Online registration of application and tracking system should be made operational at the

4
earliest so as to check the status of such applications and speedy disposal of proposals from
Micro and Small Enterprises. (Para 9 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
As informed by IBA that banks have already taken steps to identify the branches which have
more potential for financing to Micro and Small Enterprises. Banks are initiating steps for on line
registration of applications and tracking system.
The RBI has informed that the Banks have been advised vide circular dated January 4, 2012
that they should mandatorily acknowledge all loan applications, submitted manually or online, by
their MSME borrowers and ensure that a running serial number is recorded on the application form
as well as on the acknowledgement receipt. Banks are further encouraged to start Central
Registration of loan applications. The same technology may be used for online submission of loan
applications as also for online tracking of loan applications.
As regards online tracking of applications, SIDBI has taken following steps:
• The electronic loan application in Excel sheet form has since been hosted on the
website. The application form can be downloaded by the potential borrower, which can
then be forwarded electronically.
• The branches have been advised to communicate approvals like Letter of Intent,
modifications, etc. to the clients electronically.
• The status of loan applications received from the borrower is published on the website
on trial basis since December 1, 2011, via a link “know your application status”.
Further, E-tracking of applications is being developed for Prime Ministers’ Employment
Generation Programme (PMEGP), which will include the aspect of on-line registration of
applications (in addition to the option of filing a paper application).
Recommendation/observation
5. SIDBI has been created exclusively for promotion, financing and development of
MSME sector. It now operates under the administrative control of the Ministry of Finance.
The Committee feels that the Government should explore the possibility to bring SIDBI
under the Ministry of MSME so that its functions could be monitored by it for ensuring its
greater flow of credit to the MSME sector. (Para 13 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
The recommendation was taken up with the Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial
Services. Department of Financial Services has opined that SIDBI has been created exclusively for
promotion, financing and development of MSME sector. It now operates under the administrative
control of the Ministry of Finance. Ministry of Finance is alive to this role being played by SIDBI
and actively engaged in developing a suitable business plan for this Organisation. Department of
Financial Services is of the view that at present there is no need to change the supervision of
SIDBI especially where SIDBI Act is being amended in consultation with M/o MSME.
Recommendation/observation
6. When there is a dispute between entrepreneurs and banks concerning loans, the
entrepreneurs are driven from pillar to post to resolve the issue. As a matter of fact, the

5
entrepreneurs do not get relief at a reasonably short time. The Committee is of the opinion
that there should be a proper redressal mechanism at the circle level of the banks to
dispose of the cases quickly and effectively. (Para 15 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
As informed by RBI, banks have been advised vide DBOD circular dated May 5, 2003 that
their Board of Directors should lay down an appropriate grievance redressal mechanism within the
organization to resolve disputes arising in this regard. Such a mechanism should ensure that all
disputes arising out of the decisions of lending institutions’ functionaries are heard and disposed
of at least at the next higher level. The Board of Directors should also call for periodical review
of the compliance of the Fair Practices Code and the functioning of the grievances redressal
mechanism at various levels of controlling offices. A consolidated report of such reviews may be
submitted to the Board at regular intervals, as may be prescribed by it. The Fair Practices Code,
which may be adopted by banks and financial institutions, should also be put on their websites and
given wide publicity.
IBA has informed that many banks have grievance redressal mechanism at regional/circle
level for disposal of cases quickly and effectively. Banks have adopted “Code of Bank’s
Commitment to Micro and Small Enterprises”, which is being monitored by Banking Codes and
Standards Board of India (BCSBI).
Further, SIDBI has put in place a Complaints and Grievance Redressal Policy and
mechanism for attending to the complaints and grievances of the public or customer.

6
CHAPTER-II
Recommendations/Observations, which the Committee does
not desire to pursue in view of the Government's replies
Recommendation/observation
1. The Committee observes that there should be adequate delegation of powers to the
officer working at branch level. Regular meetings with MSME entrepreneurs should be
conducted and procedural formalities to procure the credit should be simplified. Besides, a
time bound action for setting up of specialised branches and conducting sample surveys
pertaining MSME accounts is required on priority. (Para 1 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
The recommendation was taken up with the Department of Financial Services and also with
the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) and Indian
Banks’ Association (IBA). However, specific information relating to adequate delegation of powers
at the branch level, regular meetings with MSME entrepreneurs and simplification of procedural
formalities for credit have not been provided. In this regard, the position is reported to be as under:
(i) As informed by the RBI, all Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) have been
advised that sufficient delegation of powers for sanction/rehabilitation of SMEs
should be made at the field level. SIDBI has also put in place a Board approved
Delegation of Powers at branch level and SIDBI holds regular meetings with
MSME entrepreneurs at cluster/ branch level. Further, IBA has informed that banks
have delegated enough powers to take decisions on the credit proposals from the
MSME entrepreneurs. The branch personnel in a routine manner explain all the
procedural formalities to procure credit to these entrepreneurs. As regards setting
up of dedicated specialized branches for MSME, individual banks have policy to
open MSME branch in potential centres.
(ii) Empowered Committees on MSMEs have been constituted at the Regional Offices of
Reserve Bank of India, under the Chairmanship of the Regional Directors with the
representatives of State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) Convenor banks, SCBs,
SIDBI, Director of Industries of the State Government, one or two senior level
representatives from the MSME Associations in the State, etc. The Committee meets
at least once in a quarter to review the credit flow to MSE sector including progress
in rehabilitation of sick MSE units. It is required to coordinate with other banks/
financial institutions and State Governments in removing bottlenecks, if any, to
ensure smooth flow of credit to the sector. At Central Office of RBI, a Standing
Advisory Committee has been constituted with Deputy Governor as Chairman,
officials of Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Banks and
Associations as members to discuss issues concerning of Micro, Small and Medium
Enterprises. The Committee examines issues relating to improving of credit to the
MSME sector, difficulties/ constraints being experienced and steps being taken to
overcome them, etc. Earlier the meetings of the Committee were on annual basis, but
now it meets twice in a year.
6

7
(iii) Public sector banks were advised in August 2005 to operationalise at least one
specialized MSE branch in every district and centre having a cluster of MSE
enterprises. So far, there were only 1220 specialised MSE branches as at the end of
March, 2011.
(iv) RBI conducts periodic studies through its Regional Offices on issues relating to MSME
credit flow.
Recommendation/observation
2. The Committee finds that the banks some time show reluctance in coming forward
to consider the credit requirement of the units under MSME sector. This attitude needs to
be changed and on the basis of the financial position of the units and their track record,
the flow of credit to MSME units should be made more smooth. (Para 2 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
In regard to the initiatives taken by banks in sensitizing their branch level functionaries on
various MSE policies, and provide them with training so as to appreciate the needs of the MSME
customers, the RBI had advised all banks to report the requisite data on trainings conducted and
MSME campaigns held. As on September 2011 public sector banks (PSBs) have conducted 1,009
trainings in the year 2011-12 and have trained 23,318 staff members. Regarding MSME campaigns,
PSBs have conducted 2,708 campaigns and granted loans to 69,421 entrepreneurs. However, the
progress in this regard needs to be monitored at the RBI level.
Further, IBA has informed that the Banks are sensitive to the development of the MSME
sector. Banks generally do not refuse credit proposals unless there are any adverse reports. If the
track records are good and financial position of the unit is good, banks definitely extend credit to
such MSME units.
Recommendation/observation
3. The Committee understands that a Task Force under the Prime Minister has
prepared and submitted a report for the overall development of the MSME sector and made
a number of recommendations. The Committee therefore recommends that these
recommendations of the Task Force should be implemented in true spirit to support the
MSME sector at the earliest so that many more entrepreneurs could be benefited.
(Para 6 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
In terms of the recommendations of the Prime Minister’s Task Force on MSMEs, the RBI
has advised the Scheduled Commercial Banks as under:
(i) Achieve a 20% year-on-year growth in credit to micro and small enterprises to ensure
enhanced credit flow;
(ii) The allocation of 60% of the MSE advances to the micro enterprises is to be achieved
in stages viz., 50 per cent in the year 2010-11, 55 per cent in the year 2011-12 and
60 per cent in the year 2012-13; and
(iii) Achieve a 10% annual growth in number of micro enterprise accounts.

8
Action has been completed in respect of a majority of recommendations of the Task Force.
Implementation of the recommendations is being monitored periodically by the Steering Group
constituted under chairmanship of Principal Secretary to Prime Minister.
Recommendation/observation
4. Revival of sick SME has to be considered with sympathy by the banks and financial
institutions. The Committee, therefore, recommends that every State Government should
come forward with a support scheme, through District Industries Centres for revival of such
units. (Para 7 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
A mechanism for rehabilitation of potentially viable sick MSEs already exists as per the
extant guidelines of RBI to Scheduled Commercial Banks. The State Level Inter Institutional
Committee (SLIIC) has been set up in each State under the Convenorship of RBI to deal with the
problems of co-ordination for rehabilitation of sick small enterprises. The Committee is presided by
Secretary, Industry of the State Government concerned. It provides a useful forum for interaction
between State Government officials and State level institutions on the one hand and term lending
institutions and banks on the other hand. Further, at the Regional Offices of RBI, Empowered
Committees (EC) have been constituted with the Regional Director of Reserve Bank as the
Chairman to review various issues relating to MSE sector particularly, the progress in MSE
financing and rehabilitation of sick MSE units and to co-ordinate with other banks/financial
institutions and the State Government in removing bottlenecks, if any, to ensure smooth flow of
credit to the sector. These Regional level Committees also decide of the need to have similar
Committees at cluster/district levels. However, since it was found that there was duplication of
deliberations at the meetings of SLIIC and Empowered Committee (EC), it was decided that the
matter of continuation or otherwise of the SLIIC forum may be left to the individual State/Union
Territory.
As reported by SIDBI, it has been extending Rehabilitation package to its assisted and
potentially viable MSME sick units which provides for relief and concessions (in the form of
reschedulement, reduction in interest rate, funding of overdue/future interest, waiver, etc.) as well
as need based additional financial assistance for their revival on viable lines.
Recommendation/observation
5. The Committee recommends that limit of the composite loan sanctioned by the Banks
and Financial Institutions should be fixed for all banks and both term loan and working
capital loan should be approved along with the project loan. (Para 10 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
RBI has reported that extant guidelines already provide for it. RBI has reiterated instructions
in this regard on March 11, 2010, that a composite loan limit of Rs.1 crore can be sanctioned by
banks to enable the MSME entrepreneurs to avail of their working capital and term loan
requirement through Single Window. As on December 2011, public sector banks have disbursed
2,84,030 composite loans amounting to Rs. 10472.05 crore.
Recommendation/observation
6. The Committee understands that the rating of the MSME sector as done by the
various credit rating agencies in co-ordination with NSIC and SIDBI should be more

9
transparent. The entrepreneur should be made to understand the shortcomings so that it
could try to improve its performance. It means that the rating scores should be discussed
with the borrower by the banker/credit rating agency without which improvement in rating
on the part of borrower would be difficult and could hinder the credit prospects and growth
of SMEs. (Para 11 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
The ‘Performance and Credit Rating Scheme’ is being implemented with a view to create
awareness amongst micro and small enterprises (MSEs) about the strengths and weakness of their
existing operations and to provide them an opportunity to enhance their organizational strengths and
credit worthiness. All rating agencies have been following a uniform rating scale based on the rating
methodology which covers a combination of credit and performance factors measuring operation,
financial, business and management risks. The rating under the scheme serves as a trusted third
party opinion on the capabilities and creditworthiness of the MSEs. As per the rating process
prescribed under the Scheme, the rating is finalized after onsite meeting with the management of
the applicant unit. A copy of the rating report, wherein strength and weaknesses of the existing
operations of the unit are explained, is also provided to the unit for its information and taking
appropriate action for the improvements.
Recommendation/observation
7. The Committee feels that to provide real advantage of finance and credit to MSME,
seminars, workshops, etc., should be organized on financial management as to enable the
MSME to effectively manage their funds, ensure regular repayments to the financial
institutions, avoid misuse of funds and prevent creation of non performing assets. It will
enable the MSME to apply for credits for establishing new ventures and expanding projects.
(Para 12 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
As informed by IBA, seminars, workshops, etc., are regularly being conducted by banks for
the benefit of the MSME borrowers.
The RBI has reported that, Banks are holding MSME campaign periodically and as per the
data submitted by Public Sector Banks (PSBs) for the quarter ended September 2011, PSBs have
conducted 2,708 campaigns and granted loans to 69,421 entrepreneurs. Further, Industry
Associations/chambers were advised to train and educate their members, if necessary with faculty
support from banks, in business planning, preparation of financial statements, etc.
Recommendation/observation
8. There is a general lack of publicity for the availability of the collateral free credit
facilities to MSME sector. The Committee, therefore, stresses upon all bankers to
prominently display the particulars of the concerned credit schemes at all the branches and
provide due publicity to them in electronic and print media. The Committee also
recommends that a campaign must be launched to spread awareness among entrepreneurs
about availability of such credit facilities. (Para 14 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
IBA has informed that the banks do display details about schemes through posters,
literatures and placement on bank’s website.

10
RBI has reported that all Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) have been advised to set up
a SME Portal on their website, where they could put in all information/products of their bank for
their MSE clients, as well as information on awareness programmes etc., organized by them. The
SCBs were also advised to understand the problem of the sector and devise strategies to gear up
their credit mechanism structure so as to achieve the prescribed target of lending to the sector.
Sensitivity on the issue to be developed at various hierarchical levels, such as, discussion of the
issue in the Board meetings, management level meetings once in three months. Branch manager’s
conference on financing to the micro sector to be held and the local NGOs, KVIC could be
involved so as to appreciate the problems of the sector and flagging major issues to remove
constraints/bottlenecks in financing. The performance of branch managers in dealing with the
sector should be made a criterion in their performance appraisal.
Further, in order to sensitise the bankers and other stakeholders, Credit Guarantee Fund
Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) cumulatively, as on March 31, 2012, has
conducted 2,953 workshops/seminars/exhibitions.
Recommendation/observation
9. As a general practice, the banks expect account holders to provide all the papers in
multiple sets and that too on several occasions. The Committee is not  happy with this
practice and urge upon all the banks to get rid of this cumbersome procedure and adopt a
simple and easy method so that entrepreneurs could apply for loans without much problem.
(Para 16 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
As informed by IBA, banks have appended check list to their loan applications to help
entrepreneurs provide all documents necessary for loan appraisal in one go.
RBI has advised all banks vide circular dated May 4, 2009 that application forms, may be
so designed that all documents required to be executed by the borrower on sanction of the loan
forms its part. The forms should invariably have a Checklist of the documents required to be
submitted by the applicant along with the application and the formalities required to be completed,
post sanction. Further, IBA has designed a uniform loan application for loans up to Rs.25 lakh and
all banks have been advised to make use of the same.

11
CHAPTER-III
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee
has either not accepted the replies of the Ministry or has asked
the Ministry to review its replies
Recommendation/observation
1. The Committee is of the opinion that the credit rating and risk assessment of the
SMEs should be taken into consideration by the bankers for reduction of their cost on loans
and structuring the rate of interest depending on the ratings. (Para 5 of ATN)
Action taken/Comments
Though the banks have their own procedure and parameters for judging the strengths and
weaknesses of an enterprise based on which they extend the credit facilities, the Evaluation Study
of the ‘Performance and Credit Rating Scheme’ for micro and small enterprises held in July, 2007
revealed that banks are giving due weightage and recognition to the rating assigned to small
enterprises.
SME Rating Agency of India Limited (SMERA), a joint initiative of SIDBI, Dun &
Bradstreet Information Services India Private Limited (D&B) and leading banks is empanelled as an
approved rating agency by the NSIC under the ‘Performance & Credit Rating Scheme’. SMERA
has been successful in entering into MoUs with 35 banks, financial institutions & trade
associations. SMERA has tied up with various banks to offer preferential interest rates to MSMEs
based on the ratings and banks internal policy.
A good rated enterprise by an independent agency strengthens its case for credit with the
bankers. Some of the banks have issued instructions to their branches to provide concessions in
interest rates based on the ratings. However, it is felt necessary that all the banks provide such
concessions to MSEs under ‘Performance and Credit Rating Scheme’.
Further Recommendation/observation
The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Government but further
recommends that it should take up the issue with Department of Financial Services to issue
guidelines regarding performance and credit rating to be followed compulsorily by the Public
Sector Banks to provide concessions in interest rates to MSMEs under the Scheme.
11

CHAPTER-IV
The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which
final replies of the Ministry have not been received
NIL

TWENTY-FOURTH REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE 
1, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry 
having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, .present this 
Twenty-Fourth Report of the Committee. The Report is on the Demands for Grants for 
1998-99 of the Department of Mines (Ministry of Steel and Mines). 
(2) The Committee at its meeting held on 22nd June, 1998, considered relevant 
documents and papers received from the Department of Mines on Demands for Grants for 
the year 1998-99 and also heard the oral evidence of the Secretary of the Department of 
Mines on the performance Budget in the context of Demands for Grants of the Department 
of Mines. 
(3) The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on 1st July, 
1998. 
(4) The Demands for Grants of the Department for the year 1998-99 as presented are as 
under:-
Plan 
Non-Plan 
Total Plan 
150.26 crore 
173.93 crore 
324.19 crore . 
(5) Taking into account the documents and other related and relevant materials made 
available to it and oral evidence tendered before it, the Committee concludes as under:-
5.1 The Department is primarily responsible for regulation and development of the 
mineral sector including the mining and metallurgy of all non-ferrous metals both in private 
and public sector except natural gas, petroleum, coal and atomic minerals. Given the natural 
resource endowments-its richness and varieties and the nation being on the threshold of 
accelerated process of industrial transformation, sustainable and planned harnessing of 
minerals are of paramount importance for rapid economic gr~wth and national development. 
The 'Privatisation Policy' has opened up the.. non-fuel ·mineral sector for private sector, the 
liberalised trade and exchange rate policy created economic opportunities and scope for 
exports and globalisation process prepared the platform for marketisation of mineral 
products in the international fora. In the absence of the specific production target for private 
sector: mining industry the Department is not in a position to make a performance budget 
analysis of their activities. As the mining sector has been opened up for foreign participation 
and Indian registered forei~:n private companies for mineral development and exploitation, 
'adequate and suitable governmental remote control-mechanism' should be evolved to 
safeguard Indian's economic interest both at domestic and international level. The 
Government should set aside "blunderbuss policy and adopt long term policy so that short­
sighted private greed does not do undue damage to the national interest. In this background 
the Committee feels that Government may consider to amend the Mineral Policy 1993 to make 
it a part and parcel of an overall industrial, trade and investment policy. 
5.2 Due to advent of mod~m technology and application of scientific approach in 
mining operation, the adoption of sophisticated and upgraded tools and equipment is not 
only the need of the hour but also indispensable for cost effective harnessing of minerals. 
The Department must think and act upon "Technology Transfer" from comparatively 

developed countries in mmmg process in order to incorporate upgraded and up-to-date 
technical know.· how into ~he mining sector. 
5.3 Infrastructural bottlenecks remained a perennial problem for all industry in general 
and mining in particular. Infrastructural network with modern means of transportation and 
communication is of paramount importance to the mining sector. The Committee 
recommends that the Department should establish and maintain a smooth Management 
Information System. The Department is· supposed to make all necessary arrangement .to invite 
foreign capital inflow to infrastructure segment of mining process whereby a part ·of the 
proceeds of mining process should be given to investing parties as repayments in a certain 
timeframe. 
5.4 The cost of mining is a subject matter of major concern of the Committee. The cost 
level in Indian mining sector in general is high due to unecomomic production level, use of 
obsolete technology, high fixed or variable costs and high break even points having an 
adverse effect on the demand of the mineral products both in the domestic and the 
international market. It will not be out of context, to mention here despite India's advantage 
of enriched endowment of aluminium resources, even without excise duty and taxes the price 
of aluminium in Indi~ are 140 per cent higher than the U.K. price which determines 
international level. In this context the Committee recommends that the Department must set 
up an expert group in each PSU to monitor, "Cost Reduction and suggest Mechanism" for 
cost reduction working upon "break-even analysis" and applying the "Boston-consulting 
Group's Experience Curve's Effect" to understand . the cost behaviour in order to have the 
maximum possible minimisation of cost; to achieve comparative competitive cost strategy to 
boost the marketisation of Indian mineral products both in domestic and international market 
on high yielding profitable price. "Break-even analysis" involving varying "Cost-Volume· 
Profit Relationship" and application of Experience Curve's Effect, with improved productivity 
of labour, increased specialisation, innovation and application of modern production 
techniques is likely to galvanise mineral exploration and exploitation process. 
5.5 Taking into account the effect of devaluation and depreciation of Indian currency, 
the Committee is constrained to express its displeasure on the marginal increase in budgetary 
allocation to the Department of Mines. Keeping in view the ambitious target of industrial 
growth rate whereby additional supply of basis; minerals are required in large volume , it is 
imperative to throw popes and aspiration towards India 's rich natural resources , and avoid 
import of minerals which will have adverse impact on India's balance _of payment. How 
much it is disastrous to be dependent upon externai aid is crystal clear with sudden and 
surprising reduction in external aict from BRGM-France. BRGM aid in 1997-98 was 
Rs. 42.50 crore which was reduced subsequently. As a result in 1997-98, the BE (Plan) of 
Rs. 154.00 crore had to be reduced to Rs. 135.60 crore in RE. BRGM .aid in the current 
financial year is Rs. 25.51 crore. As far as foreign investment is concerned sizable foreign 
capital has flown to Portfolio investment in share markets and with liberalised policy private­
investors may have long bearing impact on national interest. In order to attain the much 
acclaimed ingredients of 'self-reliance', the budgetary allocation for the Department of Mines, 
should be enhanced considerably at the time of revised estimate in 1998-99. In this regard, the 
Committ\!e reiterates its view that the Department of Mines must convince, while workinr ill 
tandem with Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission, the growing significaACe of 
Mineral exploration and development and make. necessary persuasion to have 'lion's-sh.are' in 
plan outlay to switch over from Shoe string basis of mineral exploitation to long-term strategic 
and prospective commercial exploration and development of minerals. 

5.6 In this context, Geological Survey of India (GSI) is a premier organization for 
collecting, collating and disseminating of geological data and provides basic geological 
information ensuring the continued and steady supply of raw materials to the core industrial 
sector and contributing to successful implementation of developmental programmes. 1be 
Committee notes GSI's current shift of thrust from exploration of base metal and ferrous 
group of minerals to gold and diamond, with the emerging liberalisation in Economic and 
New Mineral Policy. However, GSI's excellent expedition to marvellous objective requires 
not only recongnising GSI as an independent and scientific organization empowered with 
functional and financial autonomy but allocation of additional budgetary support to replace 
its obsolete air born geophysical system. Ocean going research vessel, survey and drilling 
equipments enabling the institution to pedorm its basic function as surveying and mapping 
and mineral exploration. Hence the need to enhance to BE of Rs. 91.50 crore in respect of 
GSI in RE for 1998-99. 
5.1 Besides GSI, Mineral Exploration Corporation Limited (MECL) is the premier 
exploration agency to carry out exploration activities on promotional basis-on behalf of 
Government of India, and contractual basis-on behalf of other agencies like public sector, 
State Government, private sector. The Committee appreciates the significant role of MECL 
in national economy through exploration of various minerals/ores by drilling and exploratory 
mining and providing reserves for eventual exploitation but the Committee is at loss to 
perceive the progressively rising trend of net loss of MECL. 
MECL could not achieve the target set for it during the 8th Plan period and the' cause for 
tbe reduced achievements have been identified as reduction in work avilability on promotional 
as well as contractual account. The Committee bas taken note of this fact and is of the opinion 
that reduction in work availability is a "managerial responsibility". Unless the management of 
MECL is geared up it will not be able to achieve the target set for its during the 9th Plan 
period and the possibilities of the company reviving and generating surplus funds in a period 
or 2-5 years will be bleak. Marginal allocation of Rs. 4.00 crore as budgetary support of 
MECL in comparison to the RE in 1997-98 (Rs. 3.80 crore) is not very encouraging, 
particularly observing the scheme/plans which are at various stages of implementation during 
1988-99. 
Various promotional projects, its successful implementation, involves capital expenditure 
like replacement of drilling accessories wh.ich is necessary to make use of the capital 
equipments and achieve targetea productivity which in tum requires huge budgetary 
allocation. The Committee appreciates MECL's efforts for making contractual negotiations 
with MEfMIN, PASMINCO and RTG, BRGM, De Beers and BHP for exploration activity 
and implementation of participation management at corporate level. 
5.8 Indian Bureau of Mines {ffiM) is a scientific and technical department primarily 
responsible for the promotion and conservation of minerals, protection of envirohment in 
mines and scientific development of mineral resources other than coal, petroleum and 
natural gas. At a time when the mining sector is confronted with maximum objection from 
the environmental · controlling agencies due to faulty implmentation of technology leading to 
major environmental degradation, the onus shifts on mM to shoulder the responsibility of 
effective mining management and environmental rehabilitation through effective 
implementation of ceo-friendly mining techniques. IBM is also required to · observe the 
international canons like Stockholm and Rio-de-Geniro Declaration of Doctrine of 
Sustainable Developmeht. To generate responsiveaess and responsibilities to mM, 
Government in general and Department of Mines in particular should ~elp the said institution 
in all aspect and in particular by higher budgetary allocation. 

Tbe Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation, to equitably distribute the 
budcetary allocation amonc GSI, mM and MECL, and further recommends that the 
Department should strive for higher budgetary allocation. 
5.9 As per the Pedonnance Budget 1998-99 the copper consumption has grown in India 
at the compound annual growth rate of around 21 per cent in 1993-94 and 1994-95 and 
around 8 per cent thereafter . The copper ore resources as on 31.3.1995 were estimated at 
732 million tonnes averaging 1.17 per cent coper. Out of this, eight working mines of 
Hindustan Copper Limited are estimated to contain 430 million tonnes of ore with an 
average grade of 1.21 per cent copper representing 58.7 per cent of the total ore resources in 
the country. But the 'sorry-state of affairs' is that HCL has projected net loss of Rs. 119.39 
a-ores in 1997-98 and Rs. 91.85 crores in 98-99 as against actual loss of Rs. 130.60 crore in 
1996-97. The loss projection in 1997-98 and 1998-99 is mainly on account of drastic fall in 
'London Metal Exchange (LME) prices of copper. Even the raising of customs duty on 
wrought copper from 30 to '35 per cent is likely, in the opinion of the Department, to get 
neutralised due to continued fall of LME prices of copper. The Department of Mines is in 
favour of a uniform enhancement of 20 per cent in the prevailing basic customs duty 
structure on impot of copper concentrates cathode, wire bar and CCR. The Committee 
observed that the production of ore, metal in concentrates, refined copper (Cathode) and 
wire rod by HCL in the preceding four years have been fluctuating. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that in order to meet the demand and supply cap 
HCL. may be advised to undertake regorous exercise on cootinuting planned scheme during 
the 9th Five Year Plan and to give enthusiastic and zealous impetus to the planned new 
schemes to arrest the continuing losses and reverse the trend by accelerating its major thrust 
areas or action in order to enable it to raise the IEBR to the tune or Rs. 685.41 crore in 
current rascal year. 
5.10 The Pedonnance Budget reveals that given the natural resources endowments, 
growing demands for aluminium and its alloys, economic opportunities and its scope for 
exports; India can produce alumina at internationally competitive prices, but the irony of the 
situation is that aluminium production rema ins short of its installed capacity.

While India's bauxite reserves account for 11 per cent of the world's deposits, our aluminium 
capacity · is only 3 per cent indicating the scope and need for new capacities to meet growing 
internal demand and sizeable exports on a long term basis. The Committee was pleased with 
the performance of some PSUs in aluminium industry like BALCO and NALCO. The 
turnover of BALCO for the year 1997-98 was Rs. 861.23 crore as against Rs. 760.56 crore in 
1996-97 while the net profit after taxes was Rs. 133.86 crore for the year 1997-98. However, 
BALCO's plant is very old and with the passage of time, the requirement of replacement or 
massive modernisation is increasing. The Committee hopes that the fund likely to be raised 
through IEBR to the tune of Rs. 140 crore would be utilised in the optimal maDDer in the 
modernisation process. 
NALCO is an integrated multilocational aluminium complex, production bauxite and 
aluminium more than the estimated target. NALCO's perspective plan for women welfare 
and welfare measures of tribals and minorities is really a subject matter of high appreciation. 
The Committee wishes its best for NALCO to keep up the performance and exporting track 
at multiplying rate. The Committee hopes that NALCO will be able to raise IEBR in 
1998-99 to the expected tune of Rs. 685.41 crore. The Committee is constrained to make an 
observation regarding the S & T Advisory Committee of NALCO on Alumina and allied 
products, Raw materials and allied products and Aluminium and allied products projects 
which had the opportunity to hold only two meetings each. At the same time, the Committee 
is satisified with the recommendations made by the S & T Advisory Committee for better 
perfomrance by NALCO and hopes that they should be implemented without delay and within 
a definite time frame. 
Related with NALCO, is the issue of disinvestment of equity of NALCO which is a 
profit-making PSU, depsite the Committee's recommendation in its 22nd report that 
disinvestment of the equity of profit making public enterprises should be undertaken with 
great circumspection. The rationale behind the stated recommendation is to protect the 
national interest and to strengthen the concept of welfare state. If the purpose of 
disinvestment is to raise the requisite capital to cope up with modernisation and technological 
upgradation in order to ntlllse the fullest installed capacity of a PSU, it is a welcome step. The 
Committee recommends that the capital so raised should be strictly and fully utilised for the 
stated purpose i.e. modernisation and technological upgradation of the PSU conceroed. 
In order to rationalise the tax structure · and to give the aluminium industry a moral 
boost, the Committee recommends the Government to pay due consideration to the demand to 
reduce the customs duty on aluminium melting scrap for recycling from 20 per cent to S per 
cent In line with steel scrap and stainless steel scrap. At the same time customs duty on un· 
wrought aluminium, aluminium ingots should be reduced to 10 per cent to encourage value­
addition. · 
5.11 The Hindustan Zinc Limited is in the forefront of the business of zinc and lead 
mining and smelting and to develop ·other natural resource-competitively. During the year 
1997-98, the Company's provisional profit is Rs. 210 crore against budgeted profit of Rs. 53 
crore. During the year 1998-99, the proposed outlay is estimated at Rs. 221.5 crore and the 
Company expects to earn a net profit of Rs: 76 crore subject to "IMF prices phenomena" 
which causes the fall in the selling prices and consequent decline in profit. The capital 
expenditure is likely to be met through internal resources and EBR viz.-suppliers credit 
and public deposits. The Committee hopes that HZL would successfully implement corporate 
plan synchronised with Five Year Plans by increasing zinc smelting capacity, augmenting lead 
zinc mining capacity, and by joint ventures with VIGEGO and BHPM. 
5.12 Sikkim Mining Corporation produces polymetallic complex ore from its Bhotang 
mine but the financial position of the corporation always remained poor due to low ore 

concentrate, erratic power supply, high transportation cost. As a matter of fact, the 
Committee recommends that Sikkim Mining Corporation requires recuperative lostrospection 
through "cost benefit analysis" and prospective overhauling. 
5.13 The Golden Past of Bharat Gold Mines is really reeling under "gloomy present and 
awaits dark future" as it is in "moribund State" which either requires 'infusion of new life' 
through substantial and sustainable rehabilitation package or 'quick winding up' Budgetary 
support of mere Rs. 6.00 crore in the year 1998-99 will be of no use to BGML. In fact, the 
BIFR has given time till 31-7-1998 for submission of a Rehabilitation scheme through 
induction of private co-promotors. It has been brought to the notice of the Committee that 
the Company has got accumulation of more than 33 million tonnes of mill-tailings at an 
average grade of 0. 7 glt and these tailings can be treated by setting up of a carbon-in-pulp 
process plant . If a new plant , based on more cost effective carbon-in-pulp process is 
installed, mill tailings can be treated more economically and can produce more than 12 
tonnes of gold over a period of 10 years. The Committee recommends that the Deaprtment 
should work on the rehabilitation scheme as suggested by BIFR on war footing so that there is 
a positive outcome within the scheduled time. The Department should also examine the 
proposal of setting up carbon-in-pulp process plant expeditiously. In the meanwhile 
Government may consider giving VRS to BGML. 
5.14 Ultimately, the Committee would like to highlights that as the workers are the real 
producers and mining process is 'risk-oriented activity', all embracing and comprehensive 
welfare measures should be taken for them in accordance with the 'Directive Principles of 
State Policy' as enshrined in the Constitution . 
5.15 The Committee hopes that the Department of Mines and the Government would 
consider and implement the recommendations of the Committee .

REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two
Hundred and Thirty-Fifth Report on the Demands for Grants (2012-13) pertaining to Ministry of
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

Recommendation/Observation

percentage to the large industries if they buy minimum percentage of goods and services from
MSMEs sector.

Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee

Recommendation/Observation
1. The Committee fails to understand the reasons behind non-utilization of funds. It is
important that the Ministry must use the money allocated to it for meeting its targets. The
Committee would like to get an explanation from the Ministry in this regard. (Para No. 14)
Action Taken/Comments
Most of the schemes of this Ministry are demand driven and hence, target for the scheme
for the forthcoming years are based on projected demands. Every MSME-DIs were assigned target
annually i.e. number of MSEs to be given benefits in their areas. Funds allocated under marketing
support scheme could not be utilized by field offices as no more MSEs having bar code
certification came forward for claiming reimbursement.
Further Recommendation/Observation
Considering the scope and role of MSME sector in national economy, such reasons
for underutilization of scarce funds betray the lack of scope and preparation before
launching such Schemes. The structure of Scheme is complex incomplete and the
implementing agencies are unable to use the resources and opportunities. Not enough effort
have been made to generate awareness about this scheme by local agencies. The Committee
is also of the view that such Schemes should have component for cost of manpower to
enable the implementing agency to high adequate and skilled manpower.
Recommendation/Observation
2. The Committee feels that the schemes discontinued could have been implemented initially on
a pilot basis. It is rather deplorable that adequate planning was not made to start such schemes
which sounded quite good. The committee feels that the plans must be devised by the Ministry by
taking into account its Vision and Mission which have been so eloquently outlined by the Ministry.
(Para No. 16)
Action Taken/Comments
This Ministry has discontinued various schemes viz. Vertical Shaft Brick Klin (VSBK),
WTO, Bio-Tech, Scheme for Tailor made courses for new entrepreneurs through select business
schools/Technical Institutes, to support 5 select universities/colleges to run 1200 Entrepreneurship
Clubs, Training cum Product Development Centres, Scheme for Capacity Building during 2012-13.
Since these schemes were having limited scope and could not achieve the desired targets, these
have been discontinued. However, by taking into the broader vision in mind, these schemes have
been subsumed into various schemes proposed in the Twelfth plan with exploring the widen
objectives and scope taking into account the vision and mission of the Ministry.

7
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee finds such replies as an attempt to discover and discard the Schemes
designed by the Ministry itself. The committee would like to be apprised as to how these
schemes have been subsumed in Twelfth Plan.

3. The Committee has taken note of the fact that the MSMEs do not have a level playing
field with the other large corporate sectors. Even the common complaint is that the tax rates are
skewed in favour of the imported items. As a result, they find it difficult to compete with the
industries which import goods from the foreign countries. This is a suggestion which deserves
serious and focused attention. The Committee would like to get a detailed explanation on this
issue. (Para No. 43)
Action Taken/Comments
The tax incidence on inputs sourced by MSMEs from domestic supplies, as compared to
the tax incidences on inputs imported by large corporate needs to be studied in order to establish
whether large corporate indeed have a cost advantage of paying lower taxes. However, it may be
noted that low tax rates on import of inputs puts pressure on domestic suppliers of inputs to
reduce prices, which in turn benefits MSMEs. The bottom line, however, is that MSMEs must
increase their competitiveness.
Government has taken several steps to increase the competitiveness of MSMEs. These
includes launching of National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP), enactment of
the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006, credit and
infrastructure support, technology up-gradation, skill development, cluster development, marketing
support and public procurement policy for micro and small enterprises.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Ministry in its reply has not addressed the issue comprehensively. The MSME
also require level playing field to remain competitive vis-à-vis low duty imports.

Recommendations/Observations in respect of which
final replies of the Ministry have not been received
Recommendation/Observation
1. The Committee strongly feels that a critical and strategic sector like the MSME deserves
higher allocations of funds from the Planning Commission. The Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh
while presenting the National Awards to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises on 28th August, 2009,
reiterated Governments’ commitment to “support, nurse and encourage this very important segment
and sector of our economy”. The sharp curtailment of the proposals of the MSME Ministry by the
Planning Commission is not in consonance with the vision of the Prime Minister to “support, nurse
and encourage this very important segment and sector of our economy”. When the country glowingly
acknowledge the vital role of MSME sector to increase productivity, enhance exports, create
employment opportunities, develop skills of our youth and promote inclusive growth, it is important
to give substantially higher allocation to the MSME Ministry. (Para No. 9)
Recommendation/Observation
2. The Committee feels that allocation of inadequate funds for the MSME Ministry is an
indication of the mind set of the concerned organization of the Government which is more aligned
to the corporate sector than the MSME sector. Given the importance of the MSME sector for our
economy, the Committee strongly recommends for the change of such mind set on the part of the
Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance for strengthening the MSME Ministry and the
MSME sector. (Para No. 10)
Action Taken/Comments on Para No. 9 and 10
Ministry of MSME proposed an outlay of Rs. 6770.40 crore for 2012-13 in its action plan
to Planning Commission. Planning Commission has assessed the requirement of funds for the year
2012-13 based on the expenditure incurred for the 2011-12 in the Eleventh Five Year Plan. As per
the record, the expenditure of M/o MSME for the year 2011-12 is Rs.1934.42 crore. M/o MSME
has been allocated a budget of Rs. 2835.00 crore for the on-going schemes including Rs. 100.00
crore for National Innovation Fund, which is 46.5% higher than expenditure done by the Ministry
during 2011-12. Thus the adequate budgetary outlay has been provided to the Ministry. This
Ministry has proposed an outlay of Rs. 64,790.00 crore for the Twelfth Plan.
Further Observation
The Committee would like to know if Ministry would require additional funds in
Supplementary Demand or has made savings. The Committee may also be informed of
quarter-wise release of Plan and Non-Plan funds.
Recommendation/observation
3. The Committee demands an explanation from the Ministry to enable it to understand the real
reasons behind such shortfall. (Para No. 12)
8

9
Action Taken/Comments
The under utilization of budgetary funds was attributed to the fact that many schemes are
demand driven. Budgetary funds could not be disbursed to beneficiaries as some of them did not
come forward to avail the benefits of some of the schemes viz.  Implementation of Lean
Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme; Promotion of ICT Tools in MSME Sector; Setting up
of Mini Tool Rooms under PPP Mode Technology; Upgradation and Quality Certification Support
to MSMEs; Support for Entrepreneurial and Managerial Development of SMEs through Incubators;
Enabling manufacturing Sector to be competitive through Quality Management Standards and
Quality Technology Tools; Marketing Assistance and Technology Upgradation and MSME cluster
development programme.
International Cooperation Scheme and Rajiv Gandhi Udyami Mitra Yojana also had their
funds underutilized for the reason of being demand driven schemes. Moreover, under the
International Cooperation Scheme, many applications could not be processed due to non-receipt of
requisite documents from the applicant organization. Under utilization of budgetary funds was also

Underutilization of funds under Khadi Reforms and Development Programme was due to

(REGP) remained largely unspent due to non-receipt of the requisite certificates from RBI and
KVIC as per the conditions laid down by the Expenditure Finance Committee and as approved by
the CCEA. The Ministry is emphasizing on RBI and KVIC that the requisite certification may be
furnished on timebound priority.
Under the Coir Sector’s ‘Rejuvenation, Modernization and Technology Upgaradation of Coir
Industry (REMOT) scheme, the funds could be only partly released as certain pre-requisites under
the scheme such as empanelment of machinery manufacturers and endline physical verification (as

5. People are queuing up to get facilities under PMEGP, but the Committee finds that the
money allocated to subsidized the margin money has not been fully utilized. The Ministry of MSME
must explain the reasons behind non-utilization of the money. (Para No. 22)
Action Taken/Comments
As per the latest available figures, the RE for margin money subsidy in 2011-12 was fully
utilized as follows:
During the year 2011-12, the Budget Estimates under Prime Minister’s Employment
Generation Programme (PMEGP) were Rs. 1037 crore [Rs.800 crore for Margin Money Subsidy
+ Rs.237 crore for Backward and Forward linkages (including Rs. 205.71 crore for residual
liabilities of erstwhile PMRY and REGP)] and the same were enhanced at Revised Estimates (RE)
stage to Rs. 1215.95 crore [Rs. 978.95 crore for Margin Money Subsidy + Rs. 237 crore for
Backward and Forward linkages (including Rs. 205.71 crore for residual liabilities of erstwhile
PMRY and REGP)]. A total of Rs. 1057.06 crore (Rs. 978.95 crore + Rs. 31.29 crore =
Rs. 1010.24 crore for Margin Money Subsidy + Rs. 46.82 crore for residual liabilities) were
released to KVIC. Rs. 31.29 crore was utilized for Margin Money Subsidy from the amount
earlier earmarked for Backward and Forward linkages. Rs. 205.71 crore – Rs. 46.82 crore =

previous year). Hence, not only the allocation of Rs. 978.95 crore for Margin Money Subsidy
in 2011-12 was released fully but additional allocation of Rs. 31.29 crore was also made from
the unutilized funds originally earmarked for Backward and Forward linkages.

The Committee notes that the annual targets for number of projects to be financed
under the Scheme have consistently been missed. What is more disconcerting is the fact
that the targets have been reduced every successive year. In year 2010-11, against a target

The Committee would like the Ministry to obtain the status report in this respect

budget of Rs. 400-500 crores. Now keeping in view the need as well requirement and potential the

As informed by RBI, MSMEs registered only as companies under the Companies Act, 1956

companies are as follows:

(ii) In hotel, hospital and software, registered companies are eligible to avail of ECBs up
to USD 200 million per financial year under the automatic route subject to compliance
with the extant guidelines on ECB; and
(iii) In other service sector other than (ii) above, they can avail of ECBs from their foreign
equity holders under the approval route.

Further Observation
The Committee may be apprised of the inputs given by Ministry of Commerce and
Industry in this regard.
Recommendation/Observation
15. The Committee takes note of the fact that the Coir Board has been allocated Rs. 7.00 crore
under Plan (Science and Technology). It feels that the amount is insufficient in the context of the
vast area of operation of the Board covering the coastal belt of the Country which includes
Lakshadweep and A&N Islands. The Committee feels that appropriate technology needs to be
transferred to the Coir Industry. It entails incubator training programmes and provision of one time
assistance upto 50% of the funds needed to establish pilot units. (Para No. 44)
Action Taken/Comments
For the Twelfth Five Year Plan, an amount of Rs.124 crore has been recommended by the
Working Group for MSME for the implementation of various programmes under the Plan (Science
and Technology) Scheme of Coir Board. The Working Group Report is yet to be considered by
the Planning Commission. An amount of Rs. 7 crore has been allocated for the implementation of
Science and Technology Scheme for the year 2012-13, which will be used in broadly the following:
1. Modernization of Production process.
2. Development of Machinery and Equipments.
3. Product Development and Diversification.
4. Development of Environment Friendly Technologies.
5. Technology Transfer, Incubation, Testing and Service Facilities.
This shall take care of the transfer of appropriate technology to the coir industry.
Further Observation
The Committee considers the allocation too meager to make any significant
difference. The Committee is also concerned about low utilization of allocation. In year

16
2011-12, for Rejuvenation, Modernization and Technology Up-gradation of Coir industry
against BE of Rs. 18.90 crores, the revised estimate was reduced to Rs. 10.53 crores. The

technology up-gradation so that allocations are fully justified.

(Para No. 49)

suggestions and recommends appropriate measures to take up these points. The Committee also
would like to get a detailed note in this regard. (Para No. 50)
Action Taken/Comments
The point-wise comments on the issues raised by the representatives of the MSME
association are given below:–
(i) Provision for the rehabilitation of sick units as large number of units are
becoming sick;
A mechanism for rehabilitation of potentially viable sick MSEs already exists as per the
extant guidelines of RBI to Scheduled Commercial Banks. The State Level Inter Institutional

17
Committee (SLIIC) has been set up in each State under the Convenorship of RBI to deal with the
problems of co-ordination for rehabilitation of sick small enterprises. The Committee is presided by
Secretary, Industry of the State Government concerned. It provides a useful forum for interaction
between State Government officials and State level institutions on the one hand and term lending
institutions and banks on the other hand. Further, at the Regional Offices of RBI, Empowered
Committees (EC) have been constituted with the Regional Director of Reserve Bank as the
Chairman to review various issues relating to MSE sector particularly, the progress in MSE
financing and rehabilitation of sick MSE units and to co-ordinate with other banks/financial
institutions and the State Government in removing bottlenecks, if any, to ensure smooth flow of
credit to the sector. These Regional level Committees also decide on the need to have similar
Committees at cluster/district levels. However, since it was found that there was duplication of
deliberations at the meetings of SLIIC and Empowered Committee (EC), it was decided that the
matter of continuation or otherwise of the SLIIC forum may be left to the individual State/Union
Territory.
Further, in order to help the sick MSMEs, SIDBI has been extending rehabilitation package
to its assisted and potentially viable MSME sick units which provides for relief and concessions
(in the form of reschedulement, reduction in interest rate, funding of overdue/future interest,
waiver, etc.) as well as need based additional financial assistance for their revival on viable lines.
SIDBI also operates a Refinance Scheme for Rehabilitation of sick small scale industrial units
assisted through primary lending institutions, viz., SFCs/SIDCs and Banks.
(ii) Appellate Authority where the problems of individual sick industry may be
heard or targets should be fixed for banks that they will have to rehabilitate
about 20% sick industries;
The modification in definition of sickness and procedure for assessing the viability is under
consideration. It is proposed to give a hearing to the MSE borrower before deciding the viability
of a unit. It is expected that once the new system is in place, the process of timely rehabilitation
of sick units would take place.
The RBI is of the view that strengthening the rehabilitation process and making it more
inclusive and effective would be in the interest of the MSE sector rather than prescribing targets,
which would lead to banks complying to achieve the target rather than putting in place an effective
monitoring and rehabilitation process of sick MSEs.
(iii) Discrimination between Small and large industries as the large industries get
protection from the Government under BIFR after erosion of 50% or more of
their net-worth but such protection is not available to sick MSEs;
As mentioned above, modification in definition of sickness and procedure for assessing the
viability is under consideration. Once the new system is in place, the process of timely
rehabilitation of sick MSE units would take place.
(iv) V enture Fund of Rs. 5000 crore should also be available to Micro Enterprises
and not only to Medium and Small Enterprises;
In order to channalise more equity funding to the MSME sector, the Union Budget
2012-13 announced setting up of a Rs. 5,000 crore India Opportunities Venture Fund (IOVF) with
SIDBI. As informed by SIDBI, the fund would be sector agnostic and utilized for providing equity
assistance to MSMEs. SIDBI would act as the Fund of Funds to help create sufficient number of
venture equity funds in the country, as also tap various channel partners like Banks, NBFCs, etc.,
apart from providing such equity/quasi-equity support directly to MSMEs.

18
(v) Enhancement of limit for MSMEs for Plan and machinery from Rs. 10 crore to
Rs. 25 crore so as to enable the MSMEs to modernize themselves;
The enhancement in the limit of small manufacturing enterprises had been made from
Rs. 1 crore to Rs. 5 crore in the year 2006. Similarly, a limit of Rs.10 crore was fixed for medium
manufacturing enterprises in the same year.
(vi) Limit of tax audit should be increased from Rs. 60 lakh to Rs. 1 crore;
In the Pre-Budget proposals 2012-13 of MoMSME it was recommended that the Tax Audit
limit may be enhanced from Rs. 60 lakh to Rs. 2 crore due to sharp increase in various input
prices resulting in inflated turnover. However, in the Union Budget 2012-13, the turnover limit for
compulsory tax audit of accounts as well as for presumptivetaxation has been raised from Rs. 60
lakh to Rs. 1 crore for SMEs.
(vii) Increasing the limit of excise duty and service tax;
The recommendation of the Committee has been taken up with the Ministry of Finance,
Department of Revenue. A reminder has been issued on 5.7.2012 and the reply is still awaited.
(viii) Enhancement of Marketing support under Marketing Development
Assistance Programme and creation of Export Development Fund;
Under MDA scheme, MSEs are encouraged to participate in International Trade fairs to
explore the export potential of their products. During the last three years (including current year)
i.e. 2010-11, 2011-12 and 2012-13, the budget allocation under this scheme was Rs. 2.40 crore,
Rs. 3.45 crore and Rs. 8.85 crore respectively.
(ix) Common Application Form for credit/loan;
As informed by RBI, IBA has designed a Uniform loan application for loans up to Rs. 25
lakh and all banks have been advised to make use of the same.
(x) Requirement of collateral security;
Banks have been mandated by RBI not to accept collateral security in the case of loans upto
Rs. 10 lakh extended to units in the MSE sector. Banks have been also advised to extend collateral-
free loans upto Rs. 10 lakh to all units financed under the Prime Minister Employment Generation
Programme of KVIC. Further, banks may, on the basis of good track record and financial position
of the MSE units, increase the limit of dispensation of collateral requirement for loans up to
Rs. 25 lakh (with the approval of the appropriate authority).
In order to encourage banks to lend more to this sector, Government of India and SIDBI
have set up the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) in July
2000, to provide credit guarantee support to collateral free/third-party guarantee free loans upto
Rs. 100 lakh extended by banks and lending institutions for micro and small enterprises (MSEs).
Cumulatively, as on March 31, 2012, 7,92,229 lakh guarantees (97% for loans below Rs. 25 lakh)
for an amount of Rs. 37,139 crore have been approved under CGS.
(xi) T ax exemption to SMEs which have separate funds for R&D;
The recommendation of the Committee has been taken up with the Ministry of Finance,
Department of Revenue.

19
(xii) Enhancement of the limit from 90 days to 6 months for NPA;
The RBI has informed that the ninety day delinquency norm has been fixed keeping in view
the international best practices and standards. All prudential norms have been prescribed with a
view to ensuring financial soundness of banks and any deviation would not be desirable.
(xiii) Enhancement of term loan from 7 years to 15 years at par with housing  sector;
The recommendation was taken up with the RBI. It has been informed that RBI has not
issued any specific instructions in this regard since the management of loan sanctioning/recovery
activity, in a bank is essentially an internal management function and each bank’s Board is
authorized to frame suitable policies. Banks have been advised to prepare a well-defined loan policy
approved by their Board of Directors which should lay down exposure limits to individual/group
borrowers, documentation standards, margin, security, sectoral exposure limits, delegation of
powers, maturity and pricing policies, factors taken into consideration for deciding interest rates
etc. Banks consider different loan proposals based on their commercial judgment and merits of
each case keeping in view the loan policies approved by their Board of Directors.
Further Observation
The Committee shall continue to study these relevant issues in its future meetings.
