35- 
CHAPTER-IV  
 
 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which fi nal replies of the Ministry 
have not been received 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The committee recognizes that Section 8 of the MSM E Development Act, 2006 
makes filing of memorandum optional for micro, smal l and those medium enterprises 
engaged in service sector. However, in view of larg e number of un-registered units, who 
are excluded from the benefits given to registered units, the committee recommends that 
registration of MSME units should be encouraged. The Ministry should make registration 
simple and non-intrusive. It should facilitate online registration of unregistered units. The 
Ministry should also take the help of industry asso ciations in this regard. The Committee 
also recommends that in addition to non-tax benefit s as announced in the Budget, tax 
benefits too should be extended to the Units who have graduated from their category. 
(Para No. 8) 
Action Taken  
 As per the instructions/guidelines at S. No. 13 of  Schedule II for Procedure of 
Filing of Entrepreneurs Memorandum and other matter s, incidental thereto, the District 
Industries Centres have to issue the acknowledgemen t for the EM filed by the enterprises 
within five days of the receipt of the form of Memo randum by post or same day, if the 
form of Memorandum is submitted in person as well as online.  
 The issue of online filing of EM has already been taken up with State 
Governments/UT Administration. While some of the St ate Govts. like Tamilnadu, 
Gujarat, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra P radesh, Uttrakhand, (EM-I), 
Jharkhand, Kerala and Assam have already implemente d online filing of EM under 
MSMED Act 2006, some State Govts. are in the process of implementing of the same. 
The recommendation for providing tax benefits upon graduation was taken up 
with the Ministry of Finance, Department of Revenue and it has been informed that the  
 
 

  
-36- 
 
recommendation is not acceptable as the tax base on  which concessions could be 
provided does not align with the criterion of inves tment that defines MSMEs in the 
MSMED Act, 2006. A case in point is service tax, wh ere tax threshold exemption is 
based on the concept of value of taxable services ( section 67 of The Finance Act, 1994) 
and not linked to investments in equipments as in the case of MSMED Act, 2006.  
 At this stage concessions can further not be provi ded owing to ongoing 
preparations for introduction of Goods and Services Tax (GST). 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 Ministry has not responded on the steps taken to e ncourage un-registered 
units to register.  Ministry may provide the information accordingly. 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee observes a steep increase in settleme nt of claims under CGTMSE 
in alternate quarters since January 2012 and would like to know the reasons for such a 
trend. 
(Para No. 28) 
Action Taken  
As informed by Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micr o and Small Enterprises 
(CGTMSE), there is substantial increase in the lodg ement of applications under Credit 
Guarantee Scheme (CGS) for seeking guarantee cover since FY 2009-10. The guarantee 
approvals have increased from Rs. 6,875 crore in FY  2010 to Rs. 12,589 crore in FY 
2011 to Rs. 13,784 crore in FY 2012 and to Rs. 16,0 62  crore in FY 2013. This 
substantial increase in guarantee approvals since F Y 2010 had consequential impact on 
the claim settlement by CGTMSE. As a sequel, while claims for the  total amount of only 
Rs. 41 crore were settled in the calendar year 2011 , claims for an amount as high as Rs. 
114 crore (almost 3 times) were settled during cale ndar year 2012. The less settlement of 
claims during the quarter April-June 2012 and Octob er-December 2012 was mainly on 
account of temporary closure of number of claims fo r want of additional information 
from Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) to enable C GTMSE to process & approve the 
claims. 

  
-37- 
Further, with the increased number of guarantee app rovals over a period of time, 
the number of claims are likely to further increase  over a period of time. It may be 
mentioned that during FY 2013 (April-March), 11,232  number of claims for Rs. 175 
crore were settled as against 1,894 number of claims for Rs. 68 crore during FY 2012. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 The Ministry has not provided the reasons for sudd en rise in guarantee 
approvals since 2010-11. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
In view of inflation, the Committee concurred with the view of Ministry to 
enhance the credit ceiling to Rs. 2 crores from existing Rs. 1 crore . 
(Para No. 34) 
Action Taken  
The recommendation was taken up with CGTMSE and the y mentioned  that 
CGTMSE has been presently operating a scheme, on pi lot basis, namely Risk Sharing 
Facility II where credits  in the range of above  R s. 100 Lakh  and  upto Rs. 200 lakh to 
eligible borrowers by designated MLIs are provided guarantee cover under World Bank 
line of credit routed through SIDBI. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 Ministry has not given details of the Risk Sharing  Facility II.  How the funds 
are to be devolved from World Bank to the borrowers through SIDBI. 
  
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The committee acknowledges and appreciates the prov ision made in the Budget 
Speech that the refinance capability of the SIDBI h as been enhance form Rs. 5000 crores 
to Rs. 10,000 crores per year.  
(Para No. 37) 
 
 
 

  
-38- 
Action Taken  
SIDBI has informed that budget announcement of enha ncing the current level of 
refinancing capability of SIDBI from the existing Rs. 5000 crore to  Rs. 10,000 crore will 
further augment the credit flow to MSME sector, and  more so, at a time when the 
economy is trying to cope up with the effects of gl obal downturn.  This is expected to 
benefit over 3.5 lakh MSEs. 
The allocation of  Rs.10,000 crore under MSE Refina nce Fund is yet to be made 
by RBI.      
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
  
      
 The Committee expresses reservation over the fact t hat despite budget 
announcement, the RBI has not made allocation under  MSE Refinance Fund.  The 
Ministry must pursue the issue with Ministry of Fin ance and RBI for expeditious 
allocation of fund.  The Committee also expects the  Ministry to explore the 
possibility if SIDBI could provide fund at concessi onal rate to NSIC for its raw 
material procurement Scheme.  
 
Recommendation/Observation                                                                                                                                          
 
The Committee observes gross under utilization in 2 011-12, when more than 
Rs.100 crores remained un-utilised. However, in the  first quarter of FY 2012-13, Rs. 211 
crore were spent, but the expenditure came down dra stically in remaining quarters of FY 
2012-13. The Ministry may information if the un-uti lised money of 2011-12 was used in 
the first quarter of 2012-13. There was under-utili sation even in 2012-13. Yet, the 
allocation has been enhanced.  The Committee seeks an explanation in this regard and 
asks the Ministry to ensure prudence in demand estimates.  
(Para No. 42) 
Action Taken  
 Out of RE of Rs. 344.30 crore for the year 2011-12 , Rs. 241.20 crore were 
allocated under General Sub-head which were fully utilized. Remaining funds were under 
NER, SCSP, and TSP Sub-heads which remained un-util ized due to non-receipt of 
proposal under these categories. However, proposals worth approximately Rs. 200 crores  
 

  
-39- 
were pending under General category apart from abov e proposals of Rs. 241.20 crore, 
which were cleared in first quarter of Financial Ye ar 2012-13 on receipt of funds general 
category (Rs. 288.60 crore). Remaining funds worth of Rs. 76.81 crore under General 
Category were utilized in 2 nd  quarter. Funds worth Rs. 22.70 crore were made ava ilable 
to CLCSS by Re-appropriation from other schemes and  were utilized in the 4th Quarter 
under General category. During financial year 2012- 13 funds woth Rs. 80 crore under 
category NER,SCSP and TSP remained mostly utilized due to non-receipt of proposal  
under these categories. No un-utilized funds of FY 2011-12 were utilized in the 1st 
quarter FY 2012-13.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 The Committee notes with reservation that funds me ant for NER remain 
unutilized.  In such cases does the money goes to n on-lapsable fund with DONER.  
The Committee recommends that the statement of DFG should specifically mention 
the allocation for NER made under every Scheme.  Th e Committee should also be 
informed if funds are allocated under each Scheme o r on the basis of aggregate 
allocation.  In any case there is an under-utilization of funds. 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee also notes that one of the major thru st of NSIC is for provide 
marketing support to the MSMEs by way of registrati on of micro and small units under 
Government Stores Purchase Programme. The Committee  however, recommends that an 
effective mechanism should be put in place to monit or the implementation of this 
important policy. 
(Para No. 55) 
Action Taken  
 NSIC operates a Single Point Registration Scheme ( SPRP) under the Government 
of Purchase Programme, wherein the registered micro  & small enterprises get benefits of 
(a) issue of Tenders free of cost, (b) Exemption fr om payment of earnest money deposit, 
(c) Price matching option to the MSEs quoting price  band of L-1 plus 15%. As per the 
Public Procurement Policy, notified vied notificati on S.O.581(E) dated 23.3.2012, every 
Central Ministry/ Department / PSU is required to set an annual goal for procurement  
 

  
-40- 
 
from the MSE sector at the beginning of the year wi th the objective of achieving an 
overall procurement goal of minimum 20% of the annu al purchases of the products or 
services produced of rendered by MSEs from the latt er in a period of three years. A 
review committee set up under the policy monitors its implementation.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 In view of the Committee’s recommendation, Ministr y may inform the 
findings/conclusion of such Review Committee.  
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 The Committee also concurs with the suggestion made  by one of the 
representative association to make mandatory for th e MNCs to source a certain 
percentage of procurement of electronic items from the MSMEs. 
(Para 56) 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
  
 The Committee is disappointed to note that the Mini stry has not forwarded 
its Action Taken/Comments on this recommendation.  The Committee, therefore, 
reiterates its earlier findings as stated in the sa id para and expects the Ministry to 
come out with a suitable action taken/reply.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The Committee appreciates the World Bank assistance  to set up 15 tool rooms 
with imported high-tech machines. The Committee als o expects the Ministry to provide 
the terms of this assistance.  Details should be pr ovided regarding the agency that will 
implement this scheme and devolution of funds to the selected tool rooms. 
(Para No. 68) 
 
 
 

  
-41- 
 
Action Taken 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Deptt. of Economic Affairs) a re concerned with external 
borrowings.  They have examined the proposal and po sed it to World Bank for 
consideration. The precise terms of World bank loan  will be known after the proposal to 
set up 15 Tool Rooms/ Technology Development Centre s during XII Plan is approved, 
and Government signs an MoU/ Agreement with World Bank. 
 The scheme will be implemented by Ministry of MSME  through societies 
(Autonomous Bodies) formed by Government. Funds for  implementation of the scheme 
will be released by Ministry of MSME to the individ ual Tool Room/ TDC separately as 
per their needs. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 The Ministry may provide terms of loan and details of MoU with World 
Bank. Whether existing individual Tool Rooms are ad ministered through 
autonomous societies.  It is surprising that budget  announcement has been made 
without deciding the terms of MoU. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
  
 However the Committee is apprehensive of the utili zation of this scheme 
considering that it has not been able to fully util ize the funds allocated under National 
Inclusive Innovation Fund. The Committee also expresses reservation that no action plan  
has yet been prepared by the despite Budget announc ement .It recommends that the 
Ministry should coordinate with the Ministry of Cor porate Affairs and Ministry of S&T, 
to get the relevant notification issued expeditiously. 
(Para No. 72) 
Action Taken  
 
 
 The funds allocated for National Inclusive Innovat ion Fund was not utilized 
during last year as the  scheme  was  not  approved  by the EFC. However, the  EFC  now  
 
 

  
-42- 
 
approved the proposal on 15.5.2013. It is expected that the fund will be utilized during 
the current financial year. 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 Ministry may inform the objective and procedure of  implementing this 
Scheme and devolution of funds to targeted beneficiaries. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
 The Committee notes Planned expenditure of Rs 1466  crore apart RE of Rs 
1402.09 crores.  Reason for such excess planned exp enditure.  The Committee notes 
increased released in first and fourth quarters and apprehends year-end rush and crowding 
of pending expenditure in first and fourth quarters .  The Committee would like further 
elaboration by the Ministry in this regard and whet her similar trend has persisted in 
previous years too. 
(Para No. 76) 
Action Taken  
The R.E. 2012-13 in respect of KVIC was Rs. 1548.79  crore (including Rs. 5.00 
crore for SFURTI) against which the planned expendi ture was to the extent of Rs. 
1466.20 crore.  It may be seen that the expenditure  is well within the allocation made 
under RE 2012-13.   
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
There is difference in figures.  Ministry has not e laborated on rush in 
expenditure during 1 st  and IV th  quarters.  
 
  
 
 The Committee suggests that the Ministry too should  intervene in resolving the 
long pending issues of MGIRI.  
(Para No. 97) 
 
 

  
-43- 
 
Action Taken 
 
Ministry gives due attention to the difficulties fa ced by MGIRI and taking active 
steps to resolve the pending issues. Necessary inst ructions /advise has already been given 
to KVIC and MGIRI to sort out the issue relating to land title.    
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 Ministry may inform of final outcome of such instr uctions and whether the 
MGIRI is now in position to utilize Budget allocation.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The Committee considers that PMEGP is an important  scheme. In view of 
significant under-achievements in meeting physical gargets, the Committee recommends 
that efforts should be made to simplify the procedu re and streamline the processes. There 
appears to be disjoint at every level of approvals.  The Committee recommends that 
DTFC should mandatorily meet and approve the applic ations at quarterly basis. And 
should evaluate the applications after due diligence. The application should be considered 
against determined check-lists and benchmarks.  The re should be time bound approval at 
every level.  It would be helpful if the DTFC assig ns local Udyami Mitras for this 
scheme.  In case of rejection the reasons should be  communicated to the applicant in 
writing within a time-limit. The KVIC alongwith the  Banks should use Bank’s publicity

PMEGP should be promoted and publicized as viable B anking product.  The Committee 
also recommends that issue of relaxing Service area  norm should be settled and notified

district  should  be  considered  as one unit.  Every approved project should automatically 
stand covered under CGTMSE however; the guarantee f ee should be absorbed by the 
Bank.  The Committee also suggests that Ministry ma y consider having a Sub-Plan for 
the revivable sick PMEGP units. 
(Para No. 129) 
 
 

  
-44- 
 
Action Taken 
 
CEO, KVIC has written to all the District Collector s in the country requesting 
them to convene DTFC meeting regularly and to dispo se off the applications received 
within 30 days of its receipt at their end.  
It has now been decided by the Ministry that one mo re member may be added in 
the Task Force to represent urban local bodies of the District, such as Municipalities and  
Nagar Palikas and amongst the three representatives from Panchayats already provided in 
the DTFC, at least one among the three Panchayat re presentatives may be nominated 
from  Scheduled  Caste  or  Scheduled  Tribe and Wo man. The  additional  representative 
from urban local bodies as mentioned above will be nominated by the Chairman/District 
Magistrate/Deputy Commissioner/Collector by rotatio n as is being done in the case of 
three Panchayat representatives.  
 
With regards to the issue relating to restriction o f service area norm of Banks, 
CEO, KVIC has written to CMDs of Public Sector Bank s requesting to consider whether 
PMEGP can be exempted from the service area norm, s o that prospective micro-
entrepreneurs find it easy to get a loan.  In addit ion, to simplify the process, KVIC has 
already started accepting PMEGP applications online.

 The Ministry may apprise the Committee on its reco mmendation regarding 
revival of PMEGP units and about joint publicity of  PMRGP with Banks.  KVIC 
State Directors should monitor the frequency of DFTC meetings and inform KVIC.

 For better and more efficient performance of the PM EGP, there was suggestion 
that was discussed in Committee that instead of giv ing the margin money, the 
Government should provide interest subvention beyon d a certain rate. Considering that 
there is a ceiling on the value of project, the tot al liability on interest rate subvention can 
be estimated. The Committee would like the Ministry  to consider this suggestion, for 
better performance of scheme.  
(Para No. 130) 

  
 
-45- 
Action Taken  
All possibilities to improve the delivery of the sc heme, including possibility for 
an interest rate subvention will be appropriately c onsidered alongwith findings of 
independent evaluations, while processing the scheme for continuation. 
 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
  
 The Ministry may inform the Committee of the terms  of reference for 
independent evaluation and the findings thereof.  T he Committee finds the Banks 
are still restrictive towards MSMEs.  This mindset needs to change.  The DLFTs 
should meet more regularly to clear the applications in time. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
  
 There is a difference between the figures for 2012 -13 as provided by the Ministry 
and those given in the Budget documents. The Commit tee reiterates its reservation over 
this recurrent trend.  The Ministry ought to reconc ile its figures as given in the 
Expenditure Budget (II) for the Ministry.  Further the Committee notes significant 
reduction in Planned allocation at RE stage to Rs 3 2.51 crores.  However, the Ministry 
released only Rs.19.31 crores to Coir Board.  It ha s been stated that the Coir Board spent 
unutilized balance of previous year.  Whether this recurrent practice of utilizing unused 
balance of previous year, in the Ministry, has the approval of Ministry of Finance. At RE 
stage only in case of Coir S&T the allocation was r etained at Rs 7 crores. However, no 
money was spent in I and III quarters and total exp enditure was Rs 2.31 crores uneven 
expenditure of Planned allocation. No money was spe nt under the important REMOT 
scheme through out the year.  The Committee feels t hat Coir industry is a promising 
sector for employment generation and export market.   While the Committee supports 
greater allocation for this Sector, it can not igno re the less than optimal performance on 
the part of Ministry and concerned agencies. These issues pertain the management, 
monitoring and financial efficiency by the Ministry and concerned agency. 
(Para No.140) 
 

  
-46- 
Action Taken  
With respect to the figures on RE and funds release d during the financial year to 
Coir Board a disparity has been noticed. RE and the  funds released for the year is Rs. 
35.51 crore and Rs. 20.07 crore respectively. 
 
Budgetary provision amounting to Rs. 700 lakh was m ade towards the scheme 
Science and Technology for the year 2012-13 in BE a nd RE. Opening balance of Rs. 
46.94 lakh was available as on 1.4.2012. Under the scheme, only an amount of Rs.231.13 
lakh was released by the Ministry. Out of which an amount of Rs. 141.67 lakh was 
released during the month of July towards 1st Quarter. No funds were released during the 
2nd & 3rd quarter against this head in spite of Boa rd's request. The restrictions imposed 
on the fund releases during March, 2013 have also c ontributed to the under utilization. 
An amount of Rs. 50 lakh towards NE and Rs. 39.47 l akh for Non NE only was released 
during March, 2013. The utilization during 2012-13 could not reach the expected level 
due to these reasons. An amount of Rs. 277.97 lakhs  has been spent upto 31.3.2012 
including NER. 
Since the 4th High Level Apex Committee meeting hel d on 20.10.20122 has 
directed that Coir Board should follow the extent p rovision of the operational guidelines 
in letter and spirit. Hence, the Board, has not rel eased any fund to the banks from 
November, 2011 to September, 2012. 
 
The Scheme of Rejuvenation, Modernization and Techn ology Upgradation of 
Coir Industry was approved by the Ministry during March, 2008 and released the fund for 
implementation of the scheme. As per the operationa l guidelines of the scheme the 
beneficiaries have to purchase machines from the em panelled machinery manufacturers 
under REMOT scheme. The first Evaluation and Steeri ng Committee meeting held on 
19.5.2008 under the Chairmanship of Chairman Coir B oard had decided to purchase coir 
machinery under REMOT scheme from the registered co ir machinery manufacturers of 
Coir Board as separate empanelled of machinery manu facture for supply of machinery 
under REMOT scheme would be time consuming and it may be delay the implementation 
of REMOT scheme. The decision of the 1 st  Evaluation and Steering Committee was 
communicated to the Ministry and also placed before  the High Level Apex Committee 
for consideration and approval. But the 4 th  High Level Apex Committee meeting held on  
 

  
-47- 
20.10.2011 while considering the amendments to the scheme operational guidelines 
directed that Coir Board should follow the extent p rovision of the operational guidelines 
in letter and spirit. Hence, the Board could not re lease any fund to the banks from 
November, 2011 onwards. Accordingly Coir Board had initiated action for empanelment 
of machinery manufacturers by inviting bids through  paper notification. Initially the 
Board could empanel only 13 machines out of 73 machines specified for the units under  
the scheme. The 9 th  Evaluation and Steering Committee meeting held on 18.4.2012 had 
decided to continue the empanelment procedure.  
 
In subsequent paper notification, Board has receive d 30 more bids for 
empanelment of machinery manufacturers under REMOT scheme. The 12th Evaluation 
and Steering Committee meeting held on 9.8.2012 has  decided to empanel 39 machinery 
manufacturers for the supply of machineries under R EMOT scheme. The empanelled list 
was forwarded to all banks and field offices of the  Board. Therefore, the Board could 
continue the implementation of the scheme from October, 2012 onwards. 
 
Further, the Banks have returned the applications to the field offices/ beneficiaries 
for submitting revised quotation from the empanelle d list. Thereafter, beneficiaries have 
submitted quotations from empanelled list and the B oard has received loan sanction 
letters from the banks during the last quarter of 2 012-13. Thus the Board had released an 
amount of Rs. 9.97 crore to the banks towards subsi dy for assisting 1147 units during the 
year 2011-12 and 2012-13 as shown below: 
 
Year No of units Subsidy released 
2011-12 170 units  Rs. 2.04 crore  
2012-13 977 units  Rs. 7.56 crore  
Total  1147 units  Rs. 9.97 crore  
 
Since the empanelment process was not completed bef ore March, 2012 the Board 
could not utilize the fund released by the Ministry  during 2011-12 and a balance amount 
of Rs. 7.97 crore was available with the Board as o n 1st April, 2012 under REMOT 
scheme. Hence, the Coir Board had requested permiss ion from the Ministry for utilizing 
the balance of previous year during the year 2012-13 and the Ministry had permitted Coir 
Board for utilizing the fund. 
 

  
-48- 
 
No release out of the budgetary allocation for 2012 -13 could be sought for due to 
the above reason and the availability of sufficient  funds with Coir Board from the 
unutilized amount for 2011-12.  
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
 The Ministry may inform the Committee of the desir ability of empanelling 
the manufacturers instead of giving freedom to entr epreneurs to purchase 
equipments from registered manufacturers.  The Comm ittee would also like to 
know the basis of such empanelment?  Whether empane lled companies offer entire 
range of equipments and provide after sale services ?  Whether it will not result in 
cartelization at a later stage.

The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to 
pursue in view of the Government's replies 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
The Committee notes that MFL, which had R&D activit ies in its early years, has 
stopped R&D activities due to consistent losses.  T he fact that Bio fertilizers of MFL 
were developed through in house R&D underlines the importance of R&D.  As the 
company has been making profits since 2009-10, the Committee is of the strong view that 
resumption of R&D activities should be one of the priorities of MFL. 
Para No. 22 
 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 
Company has informed that they would examine the fe asibility of restarting R&D 
activities . 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER–III 
The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not 
accepted the replies of the Ministry and has asked the Ministry to review its replies. 
 
 
 
Nil 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER – IV 
Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry 
have not been  received 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee notes that MFL was a profitable vent ure until 1996-97, 
barring the year 1993-94.  It is given to understan d that the Company went into the red 
owing to the problems attributed to the capacity en hancement and technology 
upgradation carried out between 1993 and 1998.  Onc e the Company stabilized its 
operations, the introduction of New Pricing Scheme for Urea Price Concession Scheme 
for complex fertilizers are said to have gone again st the interests of the MFL.  Such 
persistent problems led the Company to getting decl ared sick in April 2009.  However, 
the Committee is pleased to see MFL returning to pr ofit from 2009-10 onwards with the 
amendment of NPS-III.  It has been further noted th at a Rehabilitation Scheme, after 
taking into consideration of the inputs from Minist ries concerned, Planning Commission 
and other stakeholders has now been submitted to SB I (Operating Agency).  The 
Committee is also of the considered opinion that si nce MFL is back to making profits 
now through their efforts, it is imperative that th e Government extends a helping hand 
through a favorable approach to the Company.  Accordingly, it strongly recommends that 
the Government should expeditiously finalize the Re habilitation Scheme of MFL.  The 
Committee also expects the Government and MFL to fo cus attention on measures and 
implement them so that MFL is not allowed to slip b ack to become another sick CPSE.  
A resurgent CPSE, especially, one working in the fertilizer sector is of crucial importance 
for agricultural and economic growth of the country .  It is, therefore, necessary to 
encourage and support MFL in every way possible. 
Para No. 10 
Action Taken Reply 
MFL submitted a draft BRPSE proposal for financial restructuring seeing 
following dispensation: 
 
(i)  Write off of 40% of the GoI loan worth Rs. 221.70 Cr as on 31.03.2012 and 
the balance loan of Rs 332.54 Cr to be repaid in 10  annual installments from 
2013; 
(ii)  Waiver of GoI loan interest amounting to Rs. 234.8 5 Cr as on 31.03.2012 
along with penal interest; 
(iii) Continuation of special dispensation in prici ng mechanism under the New 
Pricing Scheme Stage-III (NPS-III) beyond 31.03.201 0 and upto conversion 
to Natural Gas; 
(iv) Continuation of additional subsidy for sourcin g “Nitrogen” through Naphtha 
based Captive Ammonia under NBS upto conversion to Natural Gas;  
(v) Exemption from applicability of Sec 41 (1) & 11 5 (j) of the Income Tax Act 
in respect of waiver granted by Banks/Institutions/ Others under revival 
scheme; 

(vi) Enhancement of retirement age from 58 years to  60 years. 
 
 The rehabilitation proposal of MFL was jointly rev iewed by Secretary 
(Fertilizers) and Secretary (BRPSE) on 4.9.2013 in order to identify a workable solution 
which would ensure long term viability of MFL. Duri ng the meeting it was brought out 
that the existing proposal of waiver of 40% GOI loa n and 100% waiver of interest on 
GOI loan may not be workable option since even thou gh it brings the company out of 
BIFR and the plant is converted to process R-LNG, i t would not be able to compete with 
new plants being set up under New Investment Policy  (NIP-2012) as its specific energy 
consumption would be much high, 7.0 Gcal/MT urea against that of 5.0 Gcal/MT Urea of 
new plants. 
 
 The company was advised to put up the alternate pr oposal of: 
  (a)  Permission to use Naphtha as feedstock till 2016-17 when Ennore 
LNG  Terminal is commissioned  
  (b) Extension of NPS –III benefits till commissio ning of Ennore Terminal  
  (c) 100% waiver of GOI loan, interest and penal i nterest (d) permission to 
invest in new large capacity Brownfield ammonia/ure a complex with the latest 
technology under NIP-2012. 
 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee observes that MFL is currently not in  a financial position to 
plan any further capacity addition or expansion sch emes.  But, it remains an indisputable 
fact that the Company could survive the slump in pe rformance in the mid-nineties solely 
due to the Revamp-cum-Modernization and Capacity En hancement of its plants.  
Accordingly, the Committee views that it is extreme ly important to take measures as 
suggested by the rehabilitation study carried out through PDIL in the year 2009.  It would 
help extend the life of plant and equipment for ano ther 15 years.  It is noted that the 
Report of PDIL suggested a capital investment of Rs . 376 crore spread over a period of 5 
years for the said technical measures.  However, it  is given to understand that the revised 
Plan Scheme for MFL envisages only on expenditure o f Rs. 150 crore during the 12 
th  
Plan Period with which the work is being executed.  In this light, it is recommended that 
MFL and the Government should take care that the te chnical measures suggested by the 
rehabilitation study conducted by PDIL in 2009 be e xecuted without fail.  It has to be 
ensured that financial constraints should not be al lowed to stand in the way of it 
implementation.  
Para No. 15 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 Against the capital investment of Rs.376.00 Crore s uggested by PDIL for 
implementing 124 schemes, MFL has already implement ed 66 schemes with an 
investment of Rs. 260.44 Crore that were sanctioned  through Plan funds during 2009-10 
to 2011-12. For the remaining 58 schemes an estimat ed amount of Rs. 150 crore needed 
and the company sought support from Department of F ertilizers for sanctioning of this 
amount through Plan funds. During 2012-13, Planning  Commission allocated an amount 

of Rs. 87.62 crore to MFL and schemes to the tune o f Rs. 87.62 crore were submitted by 
the company. But Ministry of Finance in September 2 012 imposed financial restriction 
on releasing of loan to defaulter companies and ask ed FAs of all Ministries/Departments 
to ensure that further budgetary support to default ers PSUs be considered only under 
Revival/Rehabilitation or any other scheme approved  by Cabinet. Accordingly, no funds 
were released to MFL during 2012-13. Department of Fertilizers in June 2013 also made 
a request to M/o Finance to reconsider the decision  on release of plan funds to the 
company without insisting on repayment of past loan s. However Ministry of Finance 
informed that any further assistance/releases to the PSUs will be considered only as a part 
of the revival package approved by the Cabinet. 
 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee understands that conversion of feed stock from Naphtha to 
Natural Gas is inevitability for the long-term sust ainability of Madras Fertilizers Limited.  
It is understood that cost of production of urea fr om Naphtha is very high.  While Rs. 
40,000 is required to produce one tone of urea Rs. 18,000 to Rs.19,000 required to import 
same quantity of urea.  It is in this context that conversion from Naphtha to Gas is 
essential to cut down cost of production and make t he production process more 
environments friendly.  It is understand that the M FL is almost ready for operation by 
using gas.  But it is disturbing to find that thoug h the major components of fuel switch 
over were also incorporated during the capacity enh ancement and technology up 
gradation carried during 1993 to 1998, the switch o ver has not yet materialized.  The 
initial deadline of 2009 has passed without any ach ievement as the Company relied only 
on KG D6 gas for the conversion.  The Company is su pposed to switch over to gas by 
Dec 2013.  However, it would not be possible to do so by this date.  In view of this, the 
Committee recommends that till the company switches  over to gas, it much be supplied 
with Naphtha at the rate at which gas is available.   This will help the company to 
smoothly transit from Naphtha to gas.  Therefore, t he Committee recommends that MFL 
to be proactive in this front and switch over to Na tural Gas as feedstock in the least 
possible time.  It is also recommended that the Gov ernment also has to accord priority to 
MFL in providing access to Natural Gas as the chang eover is critical to the sustainability 
of the Company itself.  The Committee is of the opi nion that the conversion of feed stock 
to Natural Gas is made part of the Rehabilitation Scheme of MFL. 
Para No. 20 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 Company has requested Indian Oil Corporation Limite d (IOCL) and Chennai 
Petroleum Corporation Limited to revisit pricing of  Naphtha, so as, to enable MFL to 
sustain operation with naphtha as feed stock till commissioning of Ennore LNG Terminal 
in 2016-17. MFL has also signed Heads of Agreement with IOCL for supply of Natural 
Gas from its Ennore LNG Terminal, when commissioned  in 2016-17. The company has 
been advised to put up a revised rehabilitation scheme taking into consideration feedstock 
conversion also. 
 
 

Further Recommendation/ observation  
 
 The Committee expects to be informed of the progres s made in the revised 
rehabilitation scheme, as submitted by the Company for the approval of the 
Cabinet.

CHAPTER – I 
 
The Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee is happy to note that many measures h ave been taken to address 
the problems including the appointment of a Chairma n cum Managing Director who has 
prepared a practical and hands on plan to revive th e Company and make it financially 
sound and profitable. The Committee strongly recommends that the management must go 
beyond core activity of the Company and consolidate , strengthen and augment its 
subsidiaries, the FACT Design and Engineering Organ ization (FEDO) and FACT 
Engineering Works (FEW) which can fetch profits and  greatly add to its financial health. 
In doing so the Company can be made a vibrant and profitable Company.   
                                                                                                                                  (Para 6) 
 
Action Taken Reply 
In order to strengthen FEDO (FACT Engineering & Des ign Organization), FACT 
is considering re-organization of FEDO for converti ng it in to a separate profit center. 
Further, efforts are on to immediately set up busin ess development offices of FEDO in 
Mumbai & Delhi, which would help FEDO to strengthen  its activities in other places 
also.  Also, discussion is on with cash rich compan ies like ONGC, EIL etc for making 
joint ventures (JVs) for the future projects of FACT, which will help FEDO to fetch more 
works related to Engineering & Consultancy. 
 
 The proposal for converting FEW (FACT Engineering Works) into a separate 
profit centre will be taken up after the FEDO exercise is through. 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
The Committee strongly recommends for the revival o f the  Company so that the 
plan envisaged by the new CMD for a turnover of  Rs .7,000 crore and a profit after tax of 
Rs.300 crore by 2020, can be  achieved by raising f ertilizer production to 20 lakh tonnes 
and fertilizer  trading to 10 lakh tonnes.                                                                 
                  (Para 14) 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 The revival proposal submitted by the Company has adopted a strategy as under: 
 
a) The improvement of  the  balance  sheet in view  of  the  substantial  
accumulated  losses  and  erosion  of  net worth. 
b) Infusion  of  additional  funds  in order  to  over come  working 
capital  constraints  for  un interrupted  operations 
c) Addressing  policy  anomalies  in  terms  of  higher  input  costs  of  
Naphtha / LNG  by  the  Government. 

d) Taking up various  projects identified  as a  part  of  its  12 th   plan  
for  medium  term  to long term  sustenance  for  w hich  support  of  GoI  is  
requested. 
 
The relief package will bring the company back on t he track of sustained operations 
and help the company generate a reasonable profit.  The package is backed up by both 
medium term and long term plans which aim to put th e company on a path of continual 
improvement in physical and financial performance. 
 
It  can  be  seen  that company  has been  making   losses mainly due to  the  inability  
to  achieve  optimal  production levels  due to  ra w material  shortage,  working capital  
limitations, high interest  burden  and inadequate  naphtha  compensation. Once these 
problems are addressed, drastic improvements in the  financial performance of the 
company are guaranteed. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER–II 
The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to 
pursue in view of the Government's replies 
Recommendation/ observation 
The Committee recommends that the above stated prob lems must be resolved by 
the Government of India for the purpose of reviving  the Company and making it 
profitable.                                                                                                                  
                    (Para 9) 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 The high cost of production is basically due to no n adequate compensation 
provided to the company on account of costly input naphtha, furnace oil and high interest 
burden on loan alongwith working capital shortage.  The Company has taken steps to 
convert its plants for the use of LNG. The hook up for conversion to LNG has been 
completed in the Ammonia plant of FACT and the plan t is under start up  utilizing LNG 
from the Petronet LNG Terminal at Kochi, which is n ow available at a landed price of 
US$ 19.5 per MMBTU. 
 The Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates are common f or all 
complex fertilizers manufacturers, and the selling prices of all similar NPK fertilizers will 
remain almost same due to the effect of market forc es. While declaring the subsidy rates 
for 2012-13, Department of Fertilizers had indicated its intension to mop up subsidy from 
companies having access to cheap natural gas.  Whil e doing so, government is 
considering that the companies who are exposed to h igher cost LNG on account of the 
location disadvantage are compensated by a suitable mechanism.     
 
For working capital and reduction of interest burde n, FACT has submitted a 
proposal for Financial restructuring of company to Department of Fertilizers. The 
Financial relief package sought for the company con sists of write off of the principal of 
the Government of India loans Rs. 282.73 crore and interest Rs. 159.17 crore accrued 
upto 31.3.2013. Besides waiver of loan and interest , company requires fresh infusion of 
fund of Rs. 300 crore as interest free loan repayab le in 10 years with a 2 year 
moratorium. The proposal for financial restructuring of FACT is now under consideration 
of Department of Fertilizers. 
 
The relief package will bring the company back on t he track of sustained 
operations and help the company generate a reasonab le profit.  The package is backed up 
by both medium term and long term plans which aim t o put the company on a path of 
improvement in physical and financial performance. These measures are included in the 
Road map for sustainability.  
 
The scheme for the revival of FACT can be categoriz ed as short term, medium term 
and long term plans. The brief details of these plans are summarized below: 
 

1) Short Term Plan- 
a) Sanctioning of the financial restructuring proposal  to prevent 
erosion of its net worth, reduce interest and ease the working capital strain. 
b) Providing a level playing field for LNG pricing by allocation of 
domestic gas or implementation of a price support mechanism. 
c) Plan fund support for essential renewals, replaceme nts & other 
schemes. 
d) Finalisation of an adequate compensation for Naphth a from 2010, 
which takes into account the increase in the price of Naphtha and furnace oil 
in place of the adhoc compensation already sanctioned. 
 
2) Medium Term Plan-  with a  focus  to ensure availab ility of raw materials and 
removal of imbalances in Intermediates  and  enhanc ing  NP  production  
capacity :- 
 
a)  Revamping the capacity of captive phosphoric acid production 
facility at Cochin division from 360 TPD to 500 TPD.  
b)  Setting up a 2000 TPD Sulphuric acid plant to redu ce imbalance in 
availability of sulphuric acid 
c)  NP expansion at Cochin division 
d)  Setting up a 3000 TPD NP Plant at Udyogamandel to replace the 
two low capacity plants presently in operation. 
e)  Setting up a 2000 TPD sulphuric acid plant at Udyo gamandel 
catering to the requirement of sulphuric acid, oleum and sulphur dioxide in the 
complex. 
 
3) Long term plans-  
 Ammonia-Urea complex at Cochin Division 
 
The combination of the relief package and the measu res highlighted in the Road map 
will ensure that the company will sustain on its ow n without external support and will

The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not

 The Committee strongly recommends that necessary s teps must be taken by 
the Government of Kerala to give land to the CWC fo r the construction of the Container 
Freight Station which will help the FACT to restore its financial and commercial viability 
and make it a profit making company.                                                                 
             (Para 11)

The 25 acres of land identified for establishment o f Container Freight 
Station in association with Central Warehousing Cor poration is a portion 
of the land acquired by the Government of Kerala un der Land Acquisition 
Act and handed over to FACT for its expansion activ ities.  FACT has paid 
compensation as well as enhanced compensation in re spect of this land. 
However, as per the Title Deed/Patta issued by the Government of Kerala, 
this land can be alienated (in this case leasing to  CWC) only with the 
permission of Government of Kerala. 
 
 FACT has approached the Government of Kerala for p ermission to lease 25 acres 
of land to CWC for establishment of Container Freig ht Station. FACT has not received 
the permission from Government of Kerala as request ed. Hence, FACT has decided to 
keep the proposal of CFS with CWC in abeyance. 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 The Committee expects to be informed of the progres s made in case of 
leasing of land to CWC by the Government of Kerala.   
 
Recommendation/ observation 
The Committee recommends that the request of the Co mpany for naphtha subsidy 
may be acceded to.                                                                                                
                  (Para 13) 
 
Action Taken Reply 
FACT is a manufacturer of the complex fertilizer gr ade NP 20:20:0:13 known by 
the trade name Factamfos and Ammonium sulphate. Und er the Nutrient Based Subsidy 
(NBS) scheme, FACT has been receiving a fixed subsi dy as per the annually notified 
rates for the nutrients N, P & S. Under the regime of floating MRP, FACT has been 
fixing the selling prices of its products in unison with other fertilizer manufacturers. 
 

FACT depends on liquid feedstock Naphtha for its pr oduction activities in the 
absence of gas availability in the region. Naphtha is a costly feedstock compared to 
natural gas. 
  
Under the NBS, in addition to the normal subsidy, t he company has been 
receiving an additional adhoc compensation for use of costly Naphtha. This 
compensation was fixed provisionally at Rs 3121 per  MT of NP & Rs 3658 per MT of 
Ammonium sulphate in the year 2010. The price of Naphtha when this compensation was 
fixed was only Rs 36000 per MT. The prices of Naphtha have continuously risen over the 
years and are above Rs 65000 per MT at present. The  finalization of the final rate of 
additional compensation for the period 2009 to 2013 for Naphtha is under process.  
 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 The Committee expects to be informed of the progres s made in the 
finalization of the final rate for naphtha subsidy.  The Committee may also be 
informed that in view of rise in Naphtha prices, wh ether there is a proposal of 
converting the plants into gas based plants  and if , the prices of gas are likely to 
remain competitive vis- a-vis naphtha.

REPORT 
 
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with  the Action Taken by the 
Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises  (Department of Heavy Industry) on 
the recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two hundred and Forty- third Report 
on the Demands For Grants (2013-14)  pertaining to Department of Heavy Industry. 
 
2.  Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Heavy Industries 
and Public Enterprises (Department of Heavy Industr y) in respect of the 
recommendations contained in the Report. These have been categorized as follows: 
 
Chapter I -  The recommendations/observations which have been  accepted by the 
Ministry. 
 The Committee is pleased to observe that the Minis try has accepted its 
recommendations as mentioned in the Chapter – I of the Report. 
 
 
Chapter -II -  The recommendations/observations which the Commi ttee does not desire 
to pursue in view of the Government's replies. 
 In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic 
and explanations advanced by the Ministry and there fore do not want to pursue them for 
the present. 
 
 
Chapter -III -  The recommendations/observations in respect of w hich the Committee has 
not accepted replies of the Ministry and has asked the Ministry to review its reply. 
 The Committee expresses its concern over the non-i mplementation of 
recommendations contained in Chapter – III and desi res that the Ministry should furnish 
logical explanations thereof. 
 
 
Chapter -IV - The recommendations/observations in respect of wh ich final replies of the 
Ministry have not been received. 
 In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either 
furnished the interim replies or couched its langua ge in vague terms therefore; the 
Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respects of 
recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention 
and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee. 
 
3. The details of the ATR are being discussed in the succeeding pages. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER – I 
 
The Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry 
 
Recommendation/observation 
 The Committee notes that during 2011-12 the Departm ent of Heavy Industry 
managed to utilize the funds allocated to them in a  relatively efficient manner. However, 
during 2012-13, the utilization of the total money allocated has not been up to the mark. 
With only a month left of the financial year, the D epartment could muster only an 
utilization of 71.40%. In view of this, the Committ ee recommends that Department of 
Heavy Industry, as the nodal department, having ove rsight of one of the most important 
sectors of the Indian industry, should improve thei r fund utilization. If the Department 
lags in this area, there can be a possible negative  cascading effect on the allocation of 
funds during the ensuing years and many important i nitiatives planned by the 
Department will be left without sufficient funding.  
                                                                                              Para No.7 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 Observation has been noted and will be complied wit h.  All efforts are being 
made to improve fund utilization in 2013-14. 
 
 
Recommendation/observation 
 The Committee strongly recommends that decision in  such matters must be taken 
on time. 
Para No.43 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 Observation has been noted and will be complied with.  
 
 
Recommendation/observation 
 The Committee commends such initiative and recommen ds that the Government must 
take measures for standardization of auto components.  
Para No.47 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 DHI is supporting UNIDO-ACMA projects which aims to  provide practical 
services to Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) for  enhancing the performance of 
domestic SMEs in the automotive component industry to facilitate their inclusion into 
national, regional and global supply chains require ments (quality, cost and delivery), to 
upgrade and enhance the competitiveness of an incre asing number of target companies 
along the supply chain in India, including lower tier suppliers. The Development Council 
of Automobile & Allied Industry (DCAAI) has also gi ven approval to Phase-I of 
UNIDO-ACMA Cluster Development Project in the year at a cost or Rs. 11.25 crore 
spread over the next three years. A MoU has been si gned between DHI, UNIDO and 
ACMA.  

CHAPTER–II 
 
The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to 
pursue in view of the Government's replies 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee observed that there are many problem s involving BHEL, 
Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd., Neyveli Lignite Corpora tion, etc. It is understood that the 
orders placed by many PSEs with BHEL are not being completed in time. As a result, 
several PSEs are not able to improve their performa nce. The Committee is constrained to 
note that the inter PSE coordination is missing. Ho wever, the Committee was informed 
by the officials of the DHI that instead of going t o the court the inter-departmental 
dispute mechanism available in the Cabinet Secretar iat may be used to sort out the issues 
among Ministries. The Committee got the assurance f rom the Secretary, DHI that he 
would look into it. The Committee strongly recommen ds that the matters involving 
several PSEs must be resolved in a time bound manne r for the completion of the projects 
and for improving the efficiency and performance of  the PSEs. The Committee would 
like to get a detailed report in this respect from the DHI. 
Para No.38 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 BHEL is currently executing an order of 6.3 MPTA e xpansion project of 
Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd. (RINL) for supply of STG  and Boiler, and an order of 2x250 
MW Circulating Fluidized Bed Combustion (CFBC) boil er based Neyveli Thermal 
Power Station (TPS)-II Expansion project of Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC). 
 
 The progress of each project is inter-alia monitor ed continuously through site 
visits by concerned officials, interaction between the project developers and various 
associated agencies / contractors / suppliers, and progress reports. In addition, regular 
review of progress of power projects is done at the  highest level in the Central Electricity 
Authority (CEA) and Ministry of Power. Furthermore,  Department of Heavy Industry 
(DHI) undertakes performance reviews of BHEL includ ing issues related to supply of 
equipment by the Company. As such, an underlying in tent of these mechanisms is for 
resolving interface issues, if any, coming in the way of project implementation. 
 
 Besides, the concept of Group Targets was envisage d in MOU of 2012-13 by the 
Department of Public Enterprises (DPE). In this reg ard, DPE “Guidelines for MoU 
between CPSE and Government Department/Ministry” states that in the circumstances of 
performances of some CPSEs being inter–dependent be cause their operations cut across 
different Ministries/Departments, MoU targets of th e concerned CPSEs should be so 
fixed that they are jointly and severally responsib le for their performance, and for 
achievement of the targets. Accordingly, group targ ets of BHEL are included with NTPC 
/ NHPC for MoU 2012-13, and with NTPC / NHPC / NLC for MoU 2013-14 comprising 
of various project milestones and targets which hav e been jointly agreed between the 
concerned CPSEs. 

 
 Additionally, a Permanent Machinery of Arbitration  (PMA) has been set up in the 
Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) since 1989 f or resolving commercial disputes, 
except taxation between CPSEs inter-se as well as b etween CPSEs and a Central 
Government Department/ Ministry/ Banks etc.  
 
 As such, the Committee on Disputes (CoD) that had been functioning in the 
Cabinet Secretariat for pursuing litigation by PSUs/Govt. Department has been wound up 
in accordance with the Order dated 17.2.2011 of the  Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in 
Civil Appeal No. 1883 of 2011 (arising out of S.L.P .(C)No. 2583 of 2009) in the case of 
Electronics Corporation of India Ltd. Vs. Union of India & others. 
 
          
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee suggested that the industry associati ons should interact with the 
educational institutions to develop curricula to mi nimize the gap between skill 
requirement and availability. The Committee also su ggested that a core group of the 
industry consisting of selected skilled people may draft educational curricula and send it 
to all educational institution for their adoption a nd incorporation in the syllabus for 
engineering students. 
Para No.45 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 DHI has apprised the Industry Associations in gener al and particularly those 
associations directly associated with different sub  sectors of domestic Capital Goods 
Industry of the observation and suggestion of the C ommittee. The skill gap study in the 
Capital Goods Sector has already been undertaken by Nation Skill Development Council. 
Representatives of the premier institutions like Indian Institute of Technology etc. will be 
co-opted as Members in the Capital Goods Skill Coun cil for development of educational 
curricula to address the issue of skill gaps. 
 
 
DHI has taken an initiative for “Formulation of Ski ll Development Plan” with a 
view to make available adequate, trained manpower f or sector like machine tools, heavy 
electrical, auto industry etc. so as to ensure prop er, streamlined and high growth rate in 
future. As far as auto sector is concerned, the tas k of identifying the skill gaps in the 
industry was undertaken through the specialized gro up formed during the framing of 
AMP 2006-16, as per which the industry is expected to require an additional 25 million 
workforce by 2016. Based on the deliberations held in the Department on various 
occasions, the Society of Indian Automobile Manufac turers (SIAM) prepared a Detailed 
Project Report (DPR). Accordingly, an Automotive Sk ill Development Council (ASDC) 
has been set up under the oversight of NSDC. An ini tial sum of Rs.75 lakh was also 
made available for the pilot project for the 1 st  year. Pilot project was implemented 
covering 3 trades related to the auto sector. The f ull project covering 24 trades in under 
submission with the NSDC. The observation has been noted for guidance and necessary 
action.    

 
 IEEMA has intimated that curriculum finalized by A ICTE is not keeping pace 
with the latest technology development. AICTE shoul d, therefore, enhance the 
involvement of industry experts in review and upgra dation of curriculum on an ongoing 
basis. 
 
 There is a need to promote greater linkage and int erface between the industry and 
academia / technical institutes, which requires con certed action by the three critical 
agencies — technical institutes, industry and government. 
 
 A Power Sector Skill Council (PSSC), proposed by C entral Electricity 
Authority (CEA) under Minister of Power, Ministry o f New & Renewable Energy 
and IEEMA, is in the process of becoming operationa l. PSSC will cover three 
distinct segments (1) Power Sector — Power Generati on, Transmission, System 
Operation and Distribution; (2) Renewable Energy Se ctor; and (3) Power 
Equipment Manufacturing Sector.  
 
 PSSC has been registered as a society under the So cieties Registration Act, 
1860, with IEEMA as one of the 7 founding members. The NSDC Board approved 
the funding assistance to the PSSC on 22n 
d August, 2013. 
 
 The objectives of PSSC are to collate and dissemin ate Labour Market 
Information; conduct research and aggregate Skill r equirements of the industry; 
create skill database; identify changing technologi es in the sector and collate 
technology specific skills; regulate the skill deve lopment activities; build capacity 
for training delivery; provide quality assurance vi a accreditation & certification; 
develop Centre of Excellence (COE).  
 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 The Ministry may apprise the Committee of the outc ome of “Formulation of 
Skill Development Plan” of DHI and also that of “Power Sector Skill Council 
(PSSC)”. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER–III 
 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not                        
accepted the replies of the Ministry and has asked the Ministry to review its                
replies 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee takes notes of the fact that funds ea rmarked for Lumpsum 
provision for the benefits of NER & Sikkim has been  going unutilized for the last two 
years. Taking cognizance of the submission of Depar tment of Heavy Industry about the 
revival plan for NPPC, the Committee recommends tha t the Department should do 
everything in its power to expedite the necessary a pprovals for the revival package for 
NPPC and consider utilizing the funds of Rs. 58.50 Crore allocated under the lumpsum 
scheme for 2013-14, for the revival of NPPC. The Co mmittee also observes that the 
trend of funds earmarked for NER gong unutilized is  highly worrisome. Considering that 
there are 4 CPSEs under Department of Heavy Industr y in the NER, it is difficult to 
conceive that there can be a dearth of proposals fo r their modernization, upgradation and 
other similar requirements. Therefore, the Committe e is of the considered opinion that 
the Department has to be more proactive for proper utilization of the funds for NER. It 
should not be a difficult task to plan the utilizat ion of the fund as it is a given fact that 
10% of Plan funds of the Department have to be set aside for the NER every year. 
Para No11 
 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) has ap proved the revival of 
NPPC and upgradation plan of NPPC through infusion of funds and increasing the 
authorized capital of NPPC from 150 Crore to 250 Cr ore. The CCEA also gave approval 
to avail term Loan of Rs.156.50 Crore from commercial Banks against Govt. Guarantee. 
 
 AYCL has informed that in view of the company’s im proved financial 
performance for the year 2010-11 and ensuing follow  on public offer, Company may not 
require any plan assistance for the scheme of plant ation and augmentation of production 
and infrastructure related facilities at Assam Tea Gardens as these can be met through 
internal resources of the Company.   
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 The reply of the Ministry is silent on the measures  adopted for improving 
utilization of NER funds.  The Committee reiterates  its recommendation of effective 
utilization of the fund earmarked for NER. Also, th e allocation of NER should be 
indicated upfront in the Expenditure Budget as also  the expenditure proposed. This 
allocation of NER should be in addition to revival /modernisation plans approved by 
the Government for the PSEs in the NER. The Committ ee finds incredible that the 
PSEs in NER do not need Budget support for their operations. 
 

Recommendation/ observation 
 
 Though the Committee takes into consideration that funds for 2011-12 (Rs. 18.30 
crore) were released in the last month of the finan cial year, it remains a fact that the 
Department could not fully utilize this amount till  November, 2012. The Department has 
quoted this under utilization as the reason for cur tailment of funds for the year 2012-13. 
In this context, the Committee is of the opinion th at if DHI faced any problem for the 
release of funds from the Ministry of Finance that could have been taken up at the 
appropriate juncture. Once funds are released there  cannot be an excuse for 
underutilization as the attainment of the defined o bjectives would be affected, especially, 
in an area as important as R&D. Further, under this  scheme till February, 2013 out of the 
Rs. 20.crore (RE), no money has been actually alloc ated. Accordingly, the Committee is 
constrained to note that the R&D has been compromis ed by not getting the amount 
released for the year 2012-13. Therefore, the Commi ttee recommends that the 
Department should take strong measures to avoid a r epetition of this mistake in future 
and impress upon the Ministry of Finance for prompt  release of funds. Also, the 
Committee is hopeful that the review of the ongoing  scheme will help the Department to 
grapple with the problems that it faced earlier.  
Para No.16 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 Observation has been noted. The amount released fro m the Cess Fund could not 
be released due to pending utilization certificate of the previous release of funds. The 
concerned organizations have been advised for timel y submission of utilization 
certificates of the previous releases, so that the further funds may be released at the 
earliest. It is further mentioned that all R&D proj ects related to automobile sector are 
cyclical in nature. Quick release of fund may not n ecessarily ensure its effective 
utilization. The new release of the funds is subjec t to the earlier released funds being 
fully utilized under the particular project. Each p roject has year-wise schedule of fund 
requirement so that annual/periodical assessment of  progress is made and a considered 
view is taken every time the Screening Committee /C ess Committee examines the status 
of the on-going projects.  
 
 However, all efforts will be made to ensure timely  utilization of funds and timely 
& periodical reviews of ongoing schemes. The Financ e Ministry will be requested for 
timely release of funds too. 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 Though the Committee takes note that the release o f funds depends on the 
furnishing of Utilization Certificates (UC) by the utilizers, the reply of the 
Government is devoid of any clear cut measures take n /to be taken for timely 
furnishing of UCs by the field organization. It is,  therefore, recommended that the 
Government should devise effective ways to encourag e and, whenever necessary, 
cajole the implementing agencies to furnish UCs in time. The Committee 
apprehends that the delayed implementation of schem es, delayed furnishing of UCs 

and resultant curtailment of funds is becoming a vi cious cycle affecting 
developmental activities. The reply appears to just ify underutilization and delay in 
realise of funds without informing the measures tak en by DHI to resolve the 
bottlenecks. 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 The Committee notes that DHI’s flagship project of  NATRiP has been severely 
plagued by delay and cost overruns. The main reason s for the delays as cited by 
Department of Heavy Industry are delay in acquisiti on of land and clearance and shifting 
of utility. Moreover, the Committee is extremely di sturbed to observe that the Actual 
expenditure year wise since 2005-06 for NATRiP has been abysmal. Barring one year 
(2008-09), the Actual expenditure has been well bel ow 50% of the corresponding RE 
figures. After an analysis of this scenario, the Co mmittee observes that the performance 
of the planning machinery for NATRiP has not been s atisfactory and lack of long term 
vision has crippled the implementation of the schem e, which has been one of the most 
awaited projects of the automobile sector. The Comm ittee recommends that at least at 
this late point in time, in comparison with the ori ginal date of completion, NATRiP 
should strictly adhere to the revised completion da te of December, 2014 and also avoid 
cost escalation in the attainment of the remaining targets.  
Para No.20 
Action Taken Reply 
 
 NATRiP has faced hurdles in the initial stages on a ccount of delays in acquisition 
of land at various sites, delays in clearances, shi fting of utilities, contractual 
complications etc. Later, after commencement of the  project, design changes on the 
original conceptual designs, due to site specific a nd equipment specific conditions also 
led to time and cost overrun. These factors led to escalation of the project cost and also 
necessitated revision in the scheduled completion d ate. The CCEA in its meeting held on 
31-04-2011 approved the revised cost of Rs. 2288 cr ore and 31 st  December, 2012 as the 
new completion date for the project and all efforts  are being made to speed up 
implementation. 
 
Further Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
 The reply of the Government gives 31/12/2012 as the  revised date of 
completion of NATRiP, which is now almost a year be hind.  The status of NATRiP 
as on date does not find a mention in it. The Commi ttee expects a more cogent reply 
in such an important matter. The lackadaisical atti tude reflecting in the reply, can 
been seen in the implementation of NATRiP also, the  effective planning and 
implementation of which could have made it much lig hter on the public exchequer 
and the result would have been cost effective.  In view of the above, the Committee 
very strongly recommends that a comprehensive upto date note on the 
implementation of NATRiP shall be furnished, showin g the present status and 
efforts taken for effective implementation after th e receipt of the Committee’s 
recommendations as contained in the 243 rd  Demands for Grant report on the 
matter.   

                                                                                                                                                                                            
Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
The Committee finds that BHEL’s IEBR figures during  2011-12, 2012-13 and 
2013-14 are at variance with the corresponding figures in expenditure budget supplied by 
DHI. Accordingly, the Committee observes that such difference in figures should have 
been reconciled with the department and thereafter presented before the Committee along 
with an explanation. The Department also, on their part should have noticed the variance 
in figures and taken it up with BHEL. 
Para No.34 
 
Recommendation/ observation 
 
 
Since, the IEBR figures BHEL are at variance, the C ommittee refrains from 
commenting on it. But the reasons quoted for the sh ortfall in IEBR figures for 2011-12 
and 2012-13 are common. The Committee observes that  the BHEL should take measures 
to address the problem which has caused shortfall. The Committee feels that the 
avoidable delay cited by the BHEL should not be all owed to spill over to another year by
